FS-01.name: Async client state read at the wrong moment or outliving its scope
FS-01.mechanism: Client code reads or captures a value before it resolves, after it goes stale, or from a store whose lifetime doesn't match the component/session: mount-time reads of async hooks, stale-closure read-modify-write toggles and URL patches, out-of-order responses, RTK data vs currentData, module-level singletons, one-shot refs/listeners never reset. Human-speed clicks on a warm cache pass; it surfaces on remount, rapid input, cold cache, StrictMode or the second open.
trigger_signals: useState/useRef seeded from a hook value that loads asynchronously (permissions, active workspace, query data)
a handler reads the current selection/URL params and writes back a modified copy, and can fire twice before re-render
a new async request per keystroke/drag with no generation token or cancellation
module-level or app-shell singleton store/cache/ref holding per-instance or per-open UI state; dialog stays mounted between opens
dependent RTK Query hooks where the first arg can change while the second is still fetching; one-shot listener keyed to an event that may already have fired
a useEffect that calls focus()/scrollIntoView lists a callback prop (onClose) that call sites pass as an inline arrow
a useEffect/useLayoutEffect reads ref.current to attach a ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver, gated on a dependency that is not the ref's own attach

an open menu, popover or dialog rendered inside a subtree that remounts on data or timer changes: TanStack column defs memoized on volatile deps with inline cell renderers, or a dialog inside an empty-state branch its own mutation flips via cache invalidation
preventive_checks: Gate queries on async ids with skipToken; use currentData/isFetching (not data/isLoading) for state scoped to a just-changed argument
Use functional updates for read-modify-write and compose URL patches into one atomic update; e2e-click two options back-to-back with no wait
Tag async requests with a monotonically increasing generation ref and drop stale resolutions; test out-of-order responses
Scope stores to the owning instance and reset state/polling on open, close and route change; test open-close-reopen and a StrictMode remount
For one-shot listeners/flags check whether the event already fired, reset on re-arm, and add a timeout fallback for any awaited cross-process signal
Depend imperative focus/scroll effects only on the triggering value (open) and hold callbacks in a ref; type into text fields with keyboard.type per keystroke in e2e, not only fill()
Attach DOM observers through a callback ref and test that resizing the observed element fires the callback

Keep column defs and cell renderers stable (volatile values via table meta/refs) and lift dialog open state above data-conditional branches; test by opening the overlay, triggering the data change, and asserting it stays open

FS-02.name: Verification against an environment not running the code under test
FS-02.mechanism: Tests or manual checks run against a server, bundle, dependency set, DB schema or measurement config that predates or differs from the code being verified: daphne/--noreload servers never restarted, Vite from another branch, reuseExistingServer adopting a foreign process, deps not reinstalled after a rebase, symlinked node_modules, unmigrated DB, Silk-enabled dev settings for query counts. The pass/fail reflects the stale environment, not the change.
trigger_signals: backend code edited, branch switched or migration added while a dev/e2e server started earlier is still running
Playwright config uses reuseExistingServer or a fixed port another worktree may hold
just rebased/merged onto a base that may add packages; fresh worktree with symlinked or missing node_modules/venv/build dirs
measuring query counts or latency via a running dev server or a bench harness with its own settings
a --keepdb test database kept across a pull that added migrations; a fresh worktree without the non-committed env file

a live e2e suite run against a backend that is 'already up' on the expected port; a fresh branch/worktree after main merged a Playwright or tooling bump; several worktrees pointing at one local sqlite file
a server for a worktree launched from another checkout's cwd while worktrees share one venv (cwd at sys.path[0] beats PYTHONPATH)
preventive_checks: Restart BE/FE servers (or confirm the process start time is newer than the last edit) before trusting any red/green result
Before e2e: confirm the ports are free or owned by this worktree (lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN), run migrate plus a health check, and reinstall deps (npm ci, pip install -e .) after any base change
Give each worktree its own real node_modules/venv; never symlink across worktrees
Measure query counts under settings.test with Silk off, assert the active settings module, and repeat timing runs
Drop/recreate the --keepdb test DB after pulling migrations, and diff a fresh worktree's env file against a known-good one before trusting a blank screen

Curl a version/health endpoint (or check the listening process's cwd and git SHA) before running a live suite against an existing server; run migrate after every branch/worktree switch; run a fresh install and `playwright install` whenever the installed versions differ from package.json
Launch servers from the worktree cwd and assert `python -c 'import pkg; print(pkg.__file__)'` points into it

FS-03.name: Code written against an assumed interface instead of the real one
FS-03.mechanism: Code, fixtures, scripts, selectors or plan snippets are written from memory or by analogy (a sibling model, a similarly named component, a library's default DOM, a unit-test mock) rather than from the actual definition: response shape, model fields, route params, hook return type, primitive API (Radix vs base-ui), field units/semantics, rendered DOM. It looks plausible, often type-checks, and fails only at runtime or in the browser.
trigger_signals: writing a parser, fixture or script against an endpoint without having printed one real response
copying a pattern from a sibling model/component whose underlying type, import path or markup differs
hand-building a route, deep link or e2e selector for a page not inspected this session
a plan snippet calls a library API or hardcodes a URL/regex/selector with no source citation
deriving a flag or scaling factor from an API field whose unit/semantics aren't documented
an ad hoc prod script or fix guesses a manager name (all_objects vs global_objects), a status value, which model an API id belongs to, or which field the FE reads

copying an RN sizing/style pattern (flexGrow: 0, fixed or percentage heights) from a component with different layout constraints; wrapping a third-party RN widget (phone input, picker) with custom overlay Views

an <a href> download/print link to an API route in an app whose auth is a bearer token in localStorage; a storage OPTIONS dict copied from another backend (S3 to GCS); a custom leading icon added to an <input type=date>; seeding records at a non-default workflow status that a human will look for
a plan or brief routes/filters at a downstream stage on a value (request host) computed and discarded upstream
a brief or plan carries verbatim implementation code the implementer is expected to paste, written in parallel with other lanes
a waitForResponse URL predicate written from the route name instead of the page's API slice endpoint
preventive_checks: Print one real response, the model definition, the .d.ts signature or the router entry before writing code against it
For e2e, inspect the real rendered DOM (roles, labels, testids) of the production component, never its unit-test mock
Trace the route to the exact component file that renders the page before editing by filename
Reuse existing URL/route builders and shared formatters instead of reconstructing them
Before a data fix or new filter, pull one real record in the target state and grep the model's managers, the serializer and the exact FE filter/conditional it must satisfy
Screenshot a new RN component, and any wrapped third-party widget against the library's own default render, before adding overlays or trusting copied sizing

Fetch protected downloads with the Authorization header into a blob URL and make the e2e follow the link; instantiate the configured storage backend with its OPTIONS in a settings test; say which tab/filter shows seeded records, or seed at the status the default view shows
Before writing a brief that routes on a value, grep the intermediate data model (CallSite) to confirm the field is carried and populated at that stage
Treat plan code as a draft: grep each cited hook, type and API in the real codebase, run the RED test first, and apply the repo's size, tenancy and lock-order rules before pasting

FS-04.name: Tests pass without proving the requirement
FS-04.mechanism: A green test cannot fail for the defect it is meant to catch: only the happy path or one of N call sites/variants is exercised, the oracle is derived from the code under test or an assumed policy, the spec adds steps the criterion doesn't allow, it asserts presence instead of content, or it encodes the current buggy behavior. Coverage numbers and green runs create false confidence until a user or reviewer hits the gap.
trigger_signals: a helper/param/pattern used at several call sites or view variants while the test plan names one
an acceptance criterion names literal text, an immediate UI change, several surfaces or several close methods
an RBAC test strips a role instead of one codename, or the permission helper has OR/tiered/owner-bypass branches
expected value computed by the same function under test, or a test comment carving out a known bug as expected
an except/error branch no existing test reaches
a spec line enumerates cases with 'or', or a test claims to exercise all N legs/branches/reasons

a unit test reads component source text or asserts a function name with toMatch(/name/); a sync pipeline carries several entity types (parent plus attached photos, voice notes, tags) through separate push/pull branches
action buttons in a fixed-width table row covered only by a click (Playwright click auto-scrolls); a spec asserting literal copy not found in the requirement it cites
a sort/order test whose fixture's insertion order already resembles the expected order; a .map(...).sort(...) chain whose comparator reads fields the mapped shape dropped

a new branch beside an existing path, a fixpoint while-changed loop, a resolver handling several AST shapes (f-string and concat), or a benchmark case labelled with a dimension (enum value, reorder) the pipeline may not capture
a plan that defers running e2e specs to a final lane, or parallel lanes merging into one integration branch
a dispatch that lists required behaviours or negative tests (audit fields, soft-delete, tenancy, sibling project, bad id) in prose
a test.skip conditioned on seed data, or a smoke test whose only assertions are URL shape and a global object
the same rule text duplicated in a doc or prompt and in a server constant
preventive_checks: Build a criterion/risk -> test table before declaring done; one test per call site and per view variant, including empty/loading/error/keyboard states
Make each acceptance e2e perform exactly the criterion's user action and assert rendered content, not element presence; an extra needed step is a product gap to report
Derive expected values from independent fixtures and cite the spec section for policy/security assertions
For permission tests read the view's permission helper and strip exactly one codename; cover OR and prerequisite branches
Force every error branch once and confirm the test fails with the fix reverted
Assert the count of legs/branches actually exercised and the exact reason string per case; build RED tests from the exact prod entity state, not a simplified repro
Assert observable output, never source-grep; require one cross-device round-trip test per synced entity type, not only the primary one

Assert toBeInViewport or a bounding box for row actions and review a full-width screenshot; source every literal copy assertion from the cited requirement or design, and flag it for clarification if absent
Give every ordering test a fixture whose insertion order contradicts the expected order, so a no-op sort fails

Mutation-test the new code before done: force the branch condition (if False:), make the loop single-pass, swap before/after fixtures or remove a different enum value, and confirm some test fails; read back written artifacts and assert on parsed content, not path or existence
Each parallel lane runs its own e2e specs and scoped tests on its own branch before merging into the integration branch; never defer all e2e execution to a final lane
Turn every behaviour a dispatch lists into named test stubs the implementer must fill, and check the names exist before accepting the task
Replace data-dependent test.skip with a fixture that creates the case; count a skipped test as missing coverage
Assert every copy of a duplicated rule (or derive one from the other) and mutation-probe by rewording each copy

FS-05.name: Concurrent sessions contend for one local DB, port, cache or CPU
FS-05.mechanism: Several agent sessions/worktrees and orphaned processes from earlier runs share the same local Postgres, pytest DB name, ports, Redis and CPU. Connection pools exhaust max_connections, test-DB create/drop races, ports get squatted and kill/cleanup hits the wrong process, so failures look like regressions in the code under test.
trigger_signals: more than one session/worktree active in the repo and about to run pytest or boot an e2e stack
e2e backend launched via daphne/runserver without DB_CONN_MAX_AGE=0, or with Silk enabled
OperationalError 'too many clients' or 'database is being accessed by other users'
re-running a command that previously timed out or was backgrounded; killing a server by its npm parent PID or lsof -ti :port
about to fan out more than about three agents that each run full Playwright suites
sizing batch/fan-out concurrency on a shared ops box; pkill -f by pattern among several agents; a hardcoded test DB name or a leftover test DB from an interrupted run
running CLI xcodebuild / expo run:ios while Xcode.app has the same project open and indexing
starting a worktree's dev servers on default ports while the primary checkout's servers are running
starting a server on a hardcoded port (API :9100, static demo :3000) that an earlier run may still hold; one agent's e2e teardown running while another agent depends on a shared dev/demo server
a reviewer or a pipelined next-task implementer dispatched with test-run permission into a lane whose implementer is still running pytest on the same per-lane test DB
parallel lanes inheriting one session scratchpad and writing helper scripts or result files with identical names
a brief that isolates ports and DBs but says nothing about scratch dirs or pattern kills; a runner that backgrounds servers with a blocking wait and no signal trap
about to fan out parallel worktree lanes, each with its own node_modules, test DBs and Playwright output, or many idle worktrees already exist
a lane wrapper passes the test command through to an agent that may drop the -n / --workers cap stated in its brief
preventive_checks: Give every parallel workstream its own PGDATABASE_TEST / e2e DB, explicit free ports and Redis prefix before dispatch
Boot e2e backends with DB_CONN_MAX_AGE=0 and Silk off; check pg_stat_activity before large runs
Before re-running, kill prior runner instances by process group and confirm none remain; target LISTEN sockets only (lsof -sTCP:LISTEN)
Wrap e2e app launches in try/finally, clean temp profiles, and cap concurrent full-suite runs per machine
Measure one job's peak RSS against free RAM before choosing concurrency; kill by the PID captured at launch; derive the test DB name per session and drop leftovers before --keepdb runs
Quit Xcode.app (or confirm it isn't open on the project) before CLI iOS builds so the two don't write one DerivedData; read the real error past exit code 65
Pick a disjoint port range for each worktree before its first server start and record it in its launch config

Record the PIDs each launch starts (pidfile) and have teardown kill only those; never kill by port range or name pattern in a multi-agent environment; check lsof -i :PORT -sTCP:LISTEN before starting and kill only that stale PID
Name test DBs per agent, not per lane, and keep profiling middleware (Silk) out of e2e backend settings
Give each lane its own scratch subdir (scratchpad/lane-X/) in the brief and have scripts assert their own lane id and port before running
Brief every lane with an explicit ban on pkill -f / killall by script name; kill only PIDs recorded in the lane's own pidfile
Write trap-based teardown (TERM, grace, KILL) with wait $pid from the start and test it by interrupting a run and checking ports are freed
Run df -h before fan-out and budget about 2 GB per worktree; between waves delete merged lanes' worktrees and node_modules and drop their test DBs
Enforce per-lane worker caps in the launcher's environment or wrapper (PYTEST_ADDOPTS with -n, a Playwright workers variable), not only as brief text, and refuse runs that exceed them

FS-06.name: Per-row queries and unbounded fetches invisible at seed scale
FS-06.mechanism: List, bulk and tree code issues a query per row (SerializerMethodField .count()/.values_list() bypassing prefetch, per-item loops inside 'bulk' endpoints, recursive per-node aggregates, per-entity external API calls), multiplies joins (sibling Count(distinct)), or fetches whole collections unpaginated. Seed data has about ten rows, so it passes review and tests until real tenants load it.
trigger_signals: a serializer gains a SerializerMethodField or helper that touches a related manager
a new bulk endpoint loops an existing per-item helper; save()/create() inside a for-loop
a queryset annotates two or more Count() over different reverse relations
tree/hierarchy aggregate, per-status count loop, or per-user external API call on a page
a new UI panel calls a list endpoint without page_size, or a response serializes the same rows twice
an org-wide scan, drift detector or batch loop over prod-scale tables (subprocess per item, __contains on an unindexed column, a full report builder called for one scalar)
a spec states a perf budget or page size while lane gates run on small or freshly bulk-inserted tables, or with a slack multiplier (a perf-slack env variable)
a save path that renumbers ordered rows (bulk_update CASE/WHEN), a heavy column written for every row of a shared save path, or FE code that generates one CSS rule per element on hundreds of nodes
an integration client that re-fetches misses with no negative cache, or a platform-wide lookup inside a per-workspace path
preventive_checks: Write a query-count test at two sizes (N=1 vs N=10) asserting it stays flat before implementing
Resolve per-row data via annotate/prefetch and iterate prefetched .all(); never .values_list() in a hot serializer path
Replace per-item loops with pk__in batch fetches, bulk_create and one GROUP BY; use Subquery instead of sibling Count(distinct)
Default new list consumers to paginated fetches, check the largest real tenant's row count, and measure real per-request latency, not only query count
EXPLAIN new filters on large tables, write detectors as one set-based query, and loop batch work inside one warm process

Seed perf fixtures at the spec's size, refresh planner statistics (ANALYZE) after seeding, gate at the page size the endpoint actually serves, no slack multipliers; keep the row mix constant across sizes in flatness checks
Run perf gates from the first perf-sensitive task onward, not in a final lane; cover insert-shaped writes as well as order-preserving ones
Frontend: toggle a class or data attribute per element instead of generating per-element selectors, and measure style recalc at spec size

FS-07.name: Parallel code paths for one operation diverge
FS-07.mechanism: The same operation or number is implemented in more than one place (single vs bulk, API create vs seed/import/duplicate, preview vs apply, immediate vs polled dispatch, list vs detail serializer, per-row cell vs summary tile). A guard, side effect, lock, scope filter or display rule added to one path is missing or different in the others, and tests cover only the primary path.
trigger_signals: adding a guard, side effect, lock or scope filter to a create/transition/update method
a bulk, seed, import, duplicate or management-command path exists alongside the primary one
a preview/count endpoint or summary tile computes the same quantity as the action or list next to it
a requirement says 'applies to all X' but X gets wired one input or one surface at a time
Django bulk_create/bulk_update/queryset.update() on a model whose save() or pre_save signals carry side effects (ledger sync, audit stamping, auto_now)
single-match vs multi-match handlers, or a required field/alert added to one caller of a shared function
adding a new state/segment variant to a list row that renders a different icon per variant

a feature adds a model or file field that a page renders while a seed/demo script builds the same data separately; a multi-write service function called from both a view (ATOMIC_REQUESTS) and a shell/command/task
adding a second resolver for the same binding kind next to one that already handles scope/shadowing

a new subtype, hold/lock state or rollout flag that must be protected across a module whose write routes (callback, retry, upload, generic CRUD, bot endpoints, service callers) all reach the same downstream path
a bulk move/visibility/delete endpoint added next to single-item actions that write audit entries
a test harness gains a new execution mode (per-worker DBs, shards, pooled seeding) while helpers resolve their own DB URL, interpreter or seed flags
a scrub, profile or sandbox applied where an artifact or CLI argv is first built, while other writers or launchers (resume and follow-up turns, group copies) build their own
preventive_checks: Grep every path that creates or mutates the model (views, bulk, seed, import, duplicate, commands) and route them through the same service method
Extract the shared rule into one function used by preview and apply; assert preview == outcome and summary == sum(rows)
Add one test per path for any new guard or side effect, and decide explicitly which side effects bulk/import paths must fire
Grep bulk_create/bulk_update/.update( on affected models and call the same sync explicitly (include auto_now fields in bulk_update); add a parity test for every sibling entry point
Give every variant the same fixed-size wrapper as its siblings and compare alignment in one screenshot

Extend the seed for every demo account and state in the same change, generate seeded files through the product's real builder, and add a reconciliation test; apply the transaction.atomic decorator on the service function itself and test it by calling it directly
When adding a sibling resolver, reuse the existing one's scope/shadow guard and test the shadowed case on both

Enumerate every write entry point that reaches the guarded state (grep URL routes and service callers), put the guard at the shared service/write entry rather than per endpoint or at a later transition, and add one test per entry point
Test that each bulk action writes one audit row per touched item, exactly like the single-item path

Resolve DB name, interpreter and seed routing in one shared harness helper used by every fixture and subprocess, and smoke every mode (1 worker, N workers, pool) asserting the DB each worker actually used
Grep every writer of the artifact and every argv builder, route them through the one function that applies the scrub or profile, and test each launcher's output

FS-08.name: E2E locator or assertion coupled to incidental page content
FS-08.mechanism: Specs locate or assert through things that are not unique or stable: copy text, unscoped getByText/role names shared with breadcrumbs, headings or a confirm dialog's trigger, substring or unanchored matches, row position/index 0 in accumulating shared data, exact computed-color strings, magic numbers, sr-only nodes. They pass once, then break or hit the wrong element as copy, data volume or browser serialization changes.
trigger_signals: the target text/name also renders in a breadcrumb, heading, sidebar, or the button that opened a confirm dialog
locator uses .first(), results[0], nth row, or a regex/name without anchors or exact:true
assertion on literal UI copy, raw API numbers, exact rgba() strings or a duplicated constant
spec expects a newly created row to be visible without searching for it
a positional assertion on a shared append-only registry; a repeated component mounted with identical testids
a Maestro assertVisible/assertNotVisible with a bare literal string on a React Native row that mixes a button and text

a computed-style assertion reached through locator('..') from a leaf-input testid; a class-based locator inside a container whose child components render the same class; money assertions with the currency glyph baked into the expected string
a Maestro tapOn by visible label text for an input on a form where the field can sit off-screen behind the keyboard
pagination is added to a list or the seed grows, while specs or helpers pick results[0], the first row, or expect a row on page 1
toHaveURL with a $-anchored regex on a route that can redirect to a default child or carry tab/filter state in the query string
navigating between two detail views of the same kind where the old panel stays mounted until the new data loads
preventive_checks: Scope locators to the owning container (dialog, row, card), go through the page driver's testids, and pass exact:true for role names
Find created entities by a unique generated identifier via search/filter, never by position
Assert through the same formatter/constant the UI uses; parse computed colors for oklab/oklch/rgb forms
Scope console-error assertions to the feature and keep known-noise allowlists in the shared helper
Dump the device accessibility hierarchy and confirm the matcher actually matches (use a regex for RN-flattened labels such as ', Add email') before trusting a RED
Locate the exact element the CSS rule selects; scope class locators to direct children (> .cls); assert the number and the currency mark separately
Tap inputs by testID/accessibilityLabel, not label text, and assert the field's value after each input step
Find the target row by id, search or filter through a driver that pages, never by position or page-1 membership; re-run specs after any seed growth, sort or page-size change
Assert a page-ready testid or match pathname only, tolerating redirect segments and query params
When a spec comment claims a row is unique ('only one active sprint'), check whether the list paginates and seed 26+ extra rows once to prove the locator still finds it
Wait for the new entity's identity marker (its id or tag) before acting, and scope locators to a container keyed by that id

FS-09.name: Green signal whose scope doesn't cover the claim
FS-09.mechanism: A check reports success without observing the claimed property: CI that lints but never builds or tests, tsc --noEmit on a references-only root, e2e files outside the type-check, a 302/200 probe answered by an SPA fallback, curl http_code on a WebSocket upgrade, a stale CI badge, a suite run before the last change, a fabricated RED step, proof screenshots overwritten or misleading. The claim ships on the strength of the signal.
trigger_signals: about to report 'verified' or 'green' from a status code, redirect, CI badge or a scoped/filtered run
the type-check/lint command differs from the project's real build command (npm run build / tsc -b)
another change landed after the last full verification run
proof screenshots written into test-results/ or a docs/qa path other runs also write
reporting a location balanced from a dry run over stored ledger rows, a single-day detector, a job's exit code, or a balance-sheet delta of 0

declaring an infra cutover or deploy done from a /health endpoint that doesn't touch the DB; reporting a multi-leg pipeline (store SDK -> backend -> app UI) as 'verified on device' after injecting synthetic data for one leg

a raw CSS edit checked only under the dev server/HMR; a completeness audit narrating another actor's capability; resuming another session's ticket where RED logs and screenshots already exist; a full-suite run that rewrites tracked screenshots of unrelated specs
the only validator reachable in a worktree without node_modules is node --check on a JSX/ESM file
an xcodebuild/gradle smoke build run without an explicitly named scheme/target and judged by exit code 0
an animation timing value copied from a design board (stagger under ~150ms) reported done without watching it run
specs that call page.screenshot({ path }) with a path inside a tracked QA-docs folder, overwriting tracked files, run by a full or sharded suite
deciding pass/fail by grepping a test runner's colored output for a summary line ('N failed', 'N passed')
preventive_checks: Run the exact project gate (npm run build, scoped pytest for touched apps) as the last step after the final change
Probe the actual property end to end: POST reaches the backend, WS returns 101 via curl -v, OAuth round-trips through the real proxy
Confirm the gate runs at all: CI has build/test jobs without continue-on-error, e2e specs are in the type-check include, a canary failure blocks
Copy proof screenshots to a unique dir immediately and git status for clobbered docs/qa files before committing
Re-run the authoritative full-range check (full rebuild / day_delta walk) and confirm expected source types (opening balances) are present before saying balanced
After cutovers hit one authenticated, DB-touching endpoint end to end and make health checks touch the DB; report verification per leg (real data / injected / unit test only)

Run the production build (next build) after CSS edits and before every deploy; cite a file:line in that actor's own code for each journey step; re-run the target suite before estimating remaining work; stage only the current change's own proof screenshots

Sanity-test any fallback validator against deliberately broken input before trusting it; treat node --check as no signal for JSX and use a real parser (esbuild/babel/eslint, or the main tree's node_modules)
Print and assert the built scheme/target and the expected output artifact, not just the exit code
Watch timed or staggered animations at runtime (screen-record or slow-mo) and map spec values to perceptible motion tokens before calling them done
Write run screenshots to testInfo.outputPath() and copy into the tracked QA-docs folder only in a deliberate proof step; run git status on that folder after every full run
Strip ANSI escapes first (sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g') or use a machine reporter (JSON/JUnit), then read the list of failed specs, not just the count; treat 'no match' as unknown, not green

FS-10.name: Interaction verified only on the mouse happy path
FS-10.mechanism: Controls work for a mouse click on the main path but fail for keyboard, focus, assistive tech or overlay stacking: unassociated labels, hover-only visibility, div rows without role/tabIndex, nested buttons, portals inside an inert modal, Escape consumed by the parent form, focus dropped by disabling the trigger, SVG labels stealing clicks, and missing empty/error/rejection states.
trigger_signals: a new clickable row, chip, chart segment, SVG node or hover-reveal control
a popover/portal rendered inside a modal, or a form-level Escape/outside-click handler
a button disabled while async work runs, or a shared Modal/Drawer reused (focus trap/restore)
a list with filters/search, a query that can skip or error, or a validation branch that can reject
a React Native return-key focus-advance chain (returnKeyType/onSubmitEditing) passes through a custom input component
a modal with a capture-phase Escape handler hosts a combobox/listbox; a disabled control whose reason is shown only through title
a nested focusable control (toggle, menu button) inside a clickable card that has its own onKeyDown; a fix removing role/tabIndex/onKeyDown from the only keyboard entry point to an action
a hand-rolled pointer drag-to-pan/resize wired only to pointerdown/pointerup
a tap handler awaits a slow device API (GPS fix, network) before flipping any visible loading or disabled state
an AC whose core action is a click, drag or selection inside rich-text editor content or a pointer-driven overlay (capture region, annotate)
a list action that removes the focused row and refetches; an aria-label passed to a control that renders its own label
preventive_checks: Tab through new UI in the e2e: every control reachable with a visible focus ring, Enter/Space activate, Escape closes the innermost overlay, focus returns to the trigger
Use the shared keyboard-accessible row/button pattern and htmlFor/id label pairs; hover-reveal via opacity, never visibility:hidden
Test empty, filtered-empty, loading, error and rejected states explicitly and give each a message
Click the real hit target in e2e (near labels, on handles), not only the testid element
List every field in order and wire each custom input's imperative focus() handle into the chain; press Next through every field on device
In e2e open the inner popup, press Escape and assert only it closes; put disabled-state reasons in aria-describedby or adjacent visible text

Nested controls stop propagation in their own key handler, tested with Enter/Space on the nested control asserting the parent handler did not fire; when removing an interactive role, substitute a real Link/button and keep the reachability test
Custom drag gestures: primary button only, preventDefault/user-select: none on start, reset on pointercancel, lostpointercapture and window blur, with a test for an interrupted drag
Flip loading/disabled UI synchronously in the press handler before any await, and test it is set in the same tick
Every pointer interaction in an editor or overlay ships its keyboard route in the same task; the plan's AC table has a keyboard row for each pointer AC
After a mutation removes the focused row, move focus to an element in the post-refetch list, and don't add aria-label on top of a self-labelling control

FS-11.name: Enumerable scope silently shrinks between ask and done
FS-11.mechanism: The scope source is a list (AC items, the sub-surfaces one criterion names, a mock's render functions and interactions, features of the component being replaced, approved-but-unbuilt specs), but the work is checked against a mental summary. Items are dropped, reduced, placeholdered or traded away and the report doesn't say so; the user finds the gap. The same gap appears as substitution: the implementer swaps in a different path or mechanism than the one the user stated, widens a guard beyond the requirement, or treats the reporter's examples as the full extent of an org-wide problem.
trigger_signals: an AC list with 6+ items, or one criterion naming several surfaces/call sites
porting from a designs/ mock or reference product, or replacing an existing page/component wholesale
a redesign that merges fields/filters or refactors shared page state with multiple URL modes
a broad go-ahead ('lets go', 'do the rest') over several approved items; a trade-off noted only in implementer notes

the user specifies an exact mechanism or scope (rebuild-only, one agent per location); a guard's docstring reads broader than the requirement; the reporter lists example entities for an org-wide issue
a store-listing or rebrand task that says 'images' or 'screenshots' (icon, feature graphic and template logos are separate slots); a 'design parity' ask with a design screenshot or jsx available
preventive_checks: Keep a literal AC -> task -> spec checklist from planning through the exit audit
Diff the build element-by-element and interaction-by-interaction against the mock render function for every view/mode before reporting done
Before replacing or consolidating UI, list every existing field, filter, affordance and mode and confirm each survives
Report any deferred, reduced or placeholder item as an explicit scope cut and ask before trading away a capability

State any deviation from an explicit directive and get one line of confirmation; wire guards against the requirement text, not the helper's docstring; run discovery unfiltered before narrowing to the reporter's examples
Enumerate every asset slot the store console exposes and every static image a template references, check each against the new brand, and bump cache-busters on swapped assets

FS-12.name: Deploy pipeline doesn't carry or match what the change needs
FS-12.mechanism: The change depends on infra the deploy doesn't provision or sync (nginx location, worker/beat unit, firewall port, env var, cache headers), or the live host has drifted from the repo (hand patches, root- or CI-user-owned files, wrong gcloud account, FE bundle built from the wrong branch, builds on the shared prod VM). The code is correct but the environment silently doesn't run it.
trigger_signals: the diff adds a URL prefix, route, service/port, Celery task or env var
the deploy script only reloads nginx/services instead of installing repo config
manual deploy on a host where CI previously ran as another OS user, or after a Docker-to-native cutover
local-build-then-ship FE deploy, or staging and prod sharing one host

a feature adds a Django migration while the target's deploy (CodeDeploy) skips migrate; a deploy hook deletes everything except an allowlist; an env var used by several systemd units; a log path change
changing a Secret-Manager-backed variable or a settings default on a VM that may also carry a local .env; rotating a secret that the service reads only at boot
settings call environ.Env.read_env() on a fixed path while deploy.sh sources the .env into the shell; a DB server provisioned on a network with a broad existing firewall rule for its port
the diff edits the deploy script that will run this very deploy (the shell executes the copy loaded before git pull)
a Node entry point calls dotenv.config() with an implicit relative path and the repo holds more than one .env file
a host migration rebuilds a venv from requirements files on a box whose old venv had hand-installed packages; several env files (admin.env, portal.env) define the same DB credential

a deploy step restores a built entrypoint from git (git checkout -- dist/index.html) instead of rebuilding, on a host where nginx serves dist/ directly; the step comes from a remembered 'standard flow' of an earlier session
a provider API key (SendGrid, SMTP2GO) is rotated or first set in prod and judged working because it authenticates

periodic or scheduled work (a Celery beat entry, a cron line) added for hosts whose deploy runs only web units and systemd timers (recurs: a scheduled sync and later an alert were both wired to a scheduler no host runs)
preventive_checks: For every new route/port/unit/env var, confirm the deploy script installs it and curl the real public path after deploy
Diff the live nginx/env config on the box against the repo before debugging routing; commit or remove hand patches
Chown deploy dirs to the deploying user and pin the gcloud account before starting
Build the FE from an explicit checkout of the target ref and verify the served asset hash; never build on the prod box (SKIP_FE_BUILD=1)

Run showmigrations / migrate --plan on the target box after any deploy carrying a migration; provision env vars into every unit that calls the helper; add a post-deploy health check that fails the pipeline
grep the live VM's .env for the same key and confirm the runtime value after restart with an authenticated request; restart every consumer right after rotating a boot-time secret

Put or symlink the .env where the library reads it as the first deploy step and run deploy.sh end to end; after provisioning, probe the DB port from outside the VM and grep postgresql.auto.conf for listen_addresses
After changing the deploy script, re-exec it after git pull or run the new step explicitly, then verify each new step's effect (query the role/table it creates) rather than a green health check
Log the resolved .env path and injected-variable count at boot, and confirm the process cwd before editing a live server's env

Before a host migration diff pip freeze on the old host against every requirements file; confirm which env file the running unit loads before provisioning a DB role, then smoke-test the real end-to-end login
Rebuild dist/ as part of the deploy, never git checkout build output, then fetch / and every asset hash it references and require 200

After rotating a provider key, fire one real call of the exact operation (send a test email) and read the key's scope list from the provider's key-info endpoint; alert on send failures rather than only logging them

Before wiring periodic work, read which scheduler the target hosts actually run (systemctl list-timers, the deploy's unit files) and register the job there; a test or deploy check asserts that scheduler invokes the entrypoint

FS-13.name: Styling correct only in the context that was eyeballed
FS-13.mechanism: Layout and style are checked at one viewport, one theme, with short seed strings and few rows, inside the page's own DOM root. Other contexts break them: long labels and many rows overflow fixed caps, ultrawide screens stretch, dark mode flips a background token but not its foreground, portaled drawers escape page-scoped selectors, cascade order or specificity overrides variants, z-index collides with the existing scale, popovers overflow without collision logic. In React Native the same happens across locales (taller Arabic text pushes a footer off a non-scrolling screen), narrow devices (an unwrapped row of links overflows its hit areas off-screen), reused shared containers (double borders) and single- vs multiline field modes.
trigger_signals: fixed px/fr column caps, fixed-size tiles, per-row heights, or height = container / rowCount
a new class scoped under a page root that may render inside a portal/drawer
a semantic background token paired with a literal text color, or a new scoped dark-mode override
a new overlay/popover z-index or anchor without collision handling

a React Native screen with localized text above action buttons and no ScrollView; a flexDirection: 'row' of tap targets without flexWrap; a shared bordered card/row container reused inside a new form; a new size variant (compact label) in a file with hardcoded offsets; a shared input row with justifyContent: 'center' now hosting a multiline TextInput
a new modal opened from a page with a fixed/sticky app-shell topbar
overriding a property set by unlayered legacy CSS with a Tailwind utility or a CSS layer rule; all: unset in unlayered feature CSS; two runtime-injected stylesheets with equal-specificity rules
a fixed-size native/desktop window or side rail hosting React content verified only in a normal browser viewport
an optional side panel added to an existing multi-column layout; 12px-or-smaller labels in a subtle/muted ink token
parallel lanes or worktrees verify UI on freshly seeded per-lane databases (few rows, short names, no history)
controls and states that render only with data: pinned or saved items, linked rows, long titles, stale or errored third-party integrations, accumulated history
preventive_checks: Screenshot at 1280, 1920 and ultrawide, in light and dark, with 3-5x seed rows and the longest realistic labels
Pair semantic background tokens with their semantic foreground; grep for text-white/text-black on flipping tokens
Grep page-root-scoped selectors used inside portaled overlays, and check the app's z-index scale before picking a value
Unit-test sizing/fit functions at maximum density and against the other constants they interact with

Screenshot RN screens in the longest-glyph locale (Arabic) and on the narrowest supported device (375pt), with the keyboard open where relevant; wrap localized content in a ScrollView, give rows of tap targets flexWrap, condition container alignment on multiline, and grep the file for hardcoded offsets when a sibling's size changes
Assert the overlay's z-index exceeds the topbar's and click the modal's own close control in e2e, not only assert visibility
Check the cascade layer of the rule you override (unlayered CSS beats every cascade layer regardless of specificity), keep feature CSS in a layer, and assert the computed style in e2e
Render the component at the host window's real size (and with long titles) in the e2e, not in a default viewport
Screenshot at 1280/1440 with every optional panel open and give the main column a min-width; run axe (serious) on new chrome and use the default ink token below 14px

Carry the 3-5x-rows / longest-labels guard into every parallel lane brief: seed each lane DB with realistic volume, long labels, pinned/saved items, linked rows and a stale integration before its sweep
Run the sweep again on the merged tree against production-like data before calling it done; a lane-only pass is not evidence for data-only controls

FS-14.name: Failure cause attributed without a controlled comparison
FS-14.mechanism: A failure is blamed on, or cleared from, the current diff, or a root cause is declared, without evidence that isolates it: no baseline run on a pristine base, truncated output read as absence, correlation instead of tracing the render path, host contention read as a regression, prod 500s with no traceback because logging isn't configured. Time is burned, or a wrong fix or claim ships.
trigger_signals: failures in files/specs the diff never touched, or right after a rebase/merge
about to say 'pre-existing', 'baseline' or 'root cause confirmed'
diagnosing from head/tail snippets, status codes, or timings on a shared machine
a prod/staging 500 or outage with no traceback or alert available
a new imbalance or residual pattern-matches a previously seen anomaly class; several subagents agree on a diagnosis

about to write a subagent's or a workaround's causal claim ('platform X can't do Y', 'the branch lacks Z') into memory or a skill; a bug report names a specific screen/flow while exploration found a similar-looking bug elsewhere
every CI job on a self-hosted host slows by a similar percentage after a network change, with no related code change
a batch of red tests labelled with one shared cause from each spec's first error line before any was reproduced or its worker DB inspected
an e2e suite carrying a known-red or baseline-red list with no owner; a flake that 'goes away' on a fresh DB or cold template and gets worked around
diagnosing from a proxy cue: a raw row count in a log/outbox table, or an ellipsis in a label read as truncation
preventive_checks: Run the identical failing set on a clean origin/<base> worktree and diff failing-test sets before attributing either way
Quote the actual traceback/log line when declaring a root cause; without one, call it a hypothesis and add logging/health checks
Grep full output instead of truncating; repeat timing measurements and check load average
Check memory for known baseline-red suites and fix them at repo level instead of re-proving them each session
Attribute the exact residual to specific ledger rows and read the posting function before naming the class; treat subagent consensus as shared anchoring, not independent evidence
Verify a causal claim against the actual branch/device before persisting it, or label it an untested hypothesis; reproduce the user's exact reported flow before fixing a look-alike
Check host-level causes first when degradation is uniform: time raw DNS lookups (dig, getent hosts) and read /etc/resolv.conf before app-level theories (sharding, pools)
For each red spec open its error-context/trace and query the worker DB at the failing step before writing a cause into a brief; label anything not reproduced as a hypothesis
Triage every red spec within the wave: fix it, or fixme it with a filed defect; never carry an unowned baseline-red list (three shipped UI regressions hid behind one)
If fresh data fixes a failure, look for pagination, ordering or accumulation over rows before blaming environment drift
Measure the user-visible unit (distinct post/message ids, not rows that include edits) and check the source/design string plus scrollWidth > clientWidth before calling a label truncated

FS-15.name: Producer and consumer of the same data disagree
FS-15.mechanism: Two sides of one data flow are defined independently and drift: FE/BE/daemon field names and envelopes, a mock's params vs the real filter, OAuth scopes in console vs code, enums duplicated across files, write-path HTML vs read-path renderer, sanitizer allowlists vs newly emitted markup, imported records vs what the read path filters on. Each side passes its own tests; only a round trip exposes the mismatch.
trigger_signals: a feature spans FE + BE (+ worker/daemon), or the FE merges ahead of its BE slice
content written into a rich-text or sanitized field, or new tags/attributes emitted
the same list of values (scopes, verbs, options, params) maintained in more than one file or system
an import/migration creates records the UI will display
a filter validates against a label map the tagger doesn't share; instructions and a helper script share a numeric parameter; parallel FE/BE agents assume a URL prefix
seeding or backfilling rows by shell script for an organization/workspace-scoped model that a mobile client pulls
a business status shown on several screens or clients (attendance Late/Absent) is reported wrong while only one client repo is open
a dataclass with to_dict/from_dict gains a field; hand-authored fixtures for a scorer that treats an unknown key as a silent non-match
FE and BE lanes or fix waves running in parallel against one contract; the FE reading a field the frozen contract doesn't have yet
one endpoint emits references (links, packets, manifests) that another endpoint resolves or validates
the same figure computed on server and client (rounding, percentages)
preventive_checks: Write a round-trip test: produce via the real producer (exact FE payload keys, the editor API), then read via the real consumer (GET, read-only renderer)
Derive enums/options/scopes from one source of truth (schema endpoint, catalogue module) instead of duplicating
Assert every FE model field is populated from a realistic API fixture; map DRF envelopes in transformResponse
When emitting new markup, check the sanitizer allowlist and renderer parity on every pipeline the field passes through
Set every scoping field the client read path filters on (organization_id) and confirm one seeded row appears end to end in the app before debugging sync
Grep where the flag is SET (not just read) across the server and every client, and fix the decision in the layer that owns it
Round-trip every new field (to_dict then from_dict) in a test, and run every new fixture through the real scorer/consumer, not only the producer-side diff
Generate TS types from the OpenAPI schema or add a parity test (codes, fields, enums) so drift fails CI; amend the contract before the FE reads a new field
Share one visibility/liveness filter between the endpoint that emits a reference and the one that resolves it, and test that every emitted reference resolves
Compute shared figures once on the server and send them; never re-derive with a different rounding rule

FS-16.name: Client-supplied id resolved outside the tenant-scoped queryset
FS-16.mechanism: An endpoint resolves a client id (list filter, nested/link route, second related id, bulk id list, polymorphic owner, reparent target, team/reviewer ids) via an unscoped get/filter, checks only one of several ids, or authorizes on the first row and writes to all. Scoping on the parent route or a sibling endpoint is assumed to cover it. Happy-path tests pass; cross-tenant tests are missing or arrive at the exit audit.
trigger_signals: the endpoint accepts <x>_id, <x>_ids, owner_type/owner_id, or a target parent/container id
a bulk endpoint authorizes once, then loops or writes over an id list
a new nested, link or relation route under an already-scoped resource
fixing an unscoped lookup in one views file while sibling files (import/export/bulk) share the pattern
an aggregate/summary computed over a wider population than the viewer's visible scope
an update serializer with fields='__all__' on a location/org-scoped model; a location header read with headers.get on a nullable FK; one payload carrying several client-controlled FKs
a serializer write helper accepts tag_ids/uuid lists and resolves them with Model.objects.get(uuid=...)
a scoped/restricted code path calls the admin/full repo method and destructures only part of its result
preventive_checks: Resolve every client id through Model.objects.for_user(user) (get_object_or_404 on the scoped queryset); never fetch-then-compare
Write the foreign-workspace/foreign-project negative test (404 for both human and bot callers) in the same commit, before implementing
In bulk endpoints scope the write queryset itself and validate all ids share one parent
When fixing one lookup, grep sibling views for get_object_or_404(Model, pk=...) and unscoped .filter(pk__in=...)
Pop scoping FKs in update(), 400 on a missing scope header, and parametrize scoping tests across every sibling endpoint and every client FK on the payload
Resolve uuids through the owner/org-scoped queryset inside serializer write helpers too, with a foreign-tenant uuid test
Give the scoped path its own narrow query and add a repo test asserting the exact columns/row shape it fetches, so PII creeping back fails

FS-18.name: Shell and CLI step semantics assumed
FS-18.mechanism: Multi-step shell work assumes semantics that don't hold: persisted cwd, bash word-splitting under zsh, GNU vs BSD tools, pipes that buffer until exit, nohup without stdin redirect, SSH jobs not detached, one stdin shared by bash -s commands, wrapper exit codes that don't propagate, git add silently staging nothing. The step 'succeeds' or appears hung and the agent proceeds on a false outcome.
trigger_signals: chained cd/source && command, or relative paths after a background/long-running command
an unquoted $VAR holding several paths in zsh; multi-line awk -v; timeout on macOS
a long remote job over SSH/gcloud, or ssh ... | bash -s with several docker exec -T calls
judging success from a wrapper's exit code, or git add with a long explicit path list
vite/vitest started in the background or piped through grep

a manage.py shell -c / < script gated on sys.argv; git add -A inside a worktree; pkill -f whose pattern is in its own argv; bash-4 syntax under macOS bash 3.2; a first command that searches from / instead of the given path

a background release/build step (gradle, xcodebuild, altool, Play upload) judged by its task notification or exit code; a script writing into a computed per-run output directory; build commands run with relative paths late in a long session
a test harness judged through `cmd | tail -N`, or a pass/fail taken from grep -c on a command's output; file tools given relative paths after Bash ran inside a worktree
a command composed as timeout N ... on a macOS host (recurs: zsh has no GNU timeout)

a GitHub Actions run: step pipes a test command into tee/grep; a shell loop over gh/git commands that prints one summary line; a python -c one-liner with quoted f-strings inside a double-quoted shell arg; a pg_restore/pg_dump flag not smoke-tested; a django.setup() one-liner run from an arbitrary cwd; git checkout -- as a mutation-test revert before any commit exists

the task prompt already gives the absolute path of the skill/context file, yet the first command is a find / or a relative path (the agent's skills directory) inside a per-run sandbox whose cwd differs from the usual checkout (recurs across parallel runs of one task, each burning the full tool timeout)
a command line interpolates a string variable holding several flags ($SSHO, $OPTS) and runs under zsh, the macOS default shell

an unquoted *, ? or [..] in a zsh command (grep --include=*.py, ls dir/*, a glob over a maybe-empty dir): zsh NOMATCH aborts the whole command instead of passing the literal through (recurs: 5x in one session)
a quoted glob handed to a program that opens paths literally (node fs, a custom script); a verification probe that regex-scrapes a port out of free-form argv/log text

a regex filter (git log --grep, grep -E) using \b or another PCRE-only escape; a reset --soft, squash or split onto a base branch tip that keeps moving; a desktop-managed shared service relaunched with open -a
supervisor code classifies a child process's run (stopped, failed, done) from its exit code after signalling it
preventive_checks: Use absolute paths and git -C <worktree>; never rely on the persisted cwd
Verify each step's effect, not its exit code: git diff --cached --stat, git log -1, grep remote logs for ERROR
Detach remote jobs with nohup/setsid plus a log file and poll; run background vite/vitest with </dev/null and --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1
Use ${=VAR} or arrays in zsh, and check command -v and the platform before relying on GNU-only tools
Gate apply flags on env vars and start prod scripts from one saved template; stage explicit paths; use bracketed pgrep patterns; read a task's given path directly and bound any search with a timeout

In build wrappers propagate child exit codes (set -e -o pipefail, PIPESTATUS), grep the output tail for BUILD FAILED/ERROR, and confirm uploads through the store API (list builds); mkdir -p output dirs before writing; run platform builds from an explicit absolute directory and make background-wait patterns match any error/failed line

Use set -o pipefail or PIPESTATUS[0] before trusting a piped result, and re-run a suspicious 'zero' without the pipe; pass absolute paths to every file tool; check git diff --cached --stat for build/output dirs before committing
On macOS never prefix with timeout; use the tool's own limit (ssh -o ConnectTimeout, jest --testTimeout) or a documented wrapper

Add set -o pipefail explicitly to piped CI run: steps and prove it by making the test fail once; print and re-verify each loop iteration's real result (gh pr view --json state); put throwaway scripts in a .py file; check unfamiliar flags with --help and verify row counts after a restore; save a commit or patch before reverting a mutation

Make the first action a Read/Skill call on the exact absolute path in the prompt; run pwd before any relative path; if discovery is unavoidable, scope find to the project or scratch dir with -maxdepth
Hold multi-flag options in an array (opts=(-o A=b -o C=d)) and pass them to ssh with quoted array expansion of all elements, or inline them; never an unquoted string variable
Quote every glob passed as an argument ('--include=*.py'), prefer rg -g, and use the (N) qualifier or setopt nullglob before listing maybe-empty paths
Never type `timeout` on this host: use the Bash tool's own timeout parameter or the runner's --timeout, and check ${pipestatus} rather than $? after a pipe
Have servers print one machine-readable line (LISTENING <port>) or pass the port explicitly; glob inside scripts rather than relying on shell expansion

Prove a search filter on a known-positive input before trusting a no-match (-P or -w instead of \b in ERE); split or squash against git merge-base HEAD origin/<base> and check git diff origin/<base>...HEAD is unchanged; after relaunching a shared local service poll its health (docker info, pg_isready) and kill leftover helper PIDs if the relaunch did nothing
Record the stop reason before signalling a child process and classify the outcome from that record; test children that exit 0 and non-zero after SIGINT

FS-19.name: Behavior change leaves dependent tests, drivers and mocks stale
FS-19.mechanism: A component's interaction model, a response shape, a default value, a permission class or a shared fixture changes, but the unit tests, MSW handlers, e2e drivers, seed helpers and specs that encoded the old behavior are not updated in the same change. With CI not running those suites they go silently red, and later sessions misread them as their own regressions or as baseline noise.
trigger_signals: a shared component gains a hook, a confirm/apply step, a new underlying library, or a new default layout/copy
a response shape changes (bare list -> paginated envelope) or a query hook moves to a scoped endpoint
a default param value, permission class, or auto-provisioning behavior changes
a stubbed fixture's real endpoint ships
a permission class added to an existing endpoint; a patched symbol moved or renamed while tests use mock.patch string paths

swapping a field's control type (Input to Select), flipping a form's default enum value, replacing a placeholder/disabled state with the shipped feature, or a global render change (currency glyph to SVG, exotic whitespace, DS required-asterisk markup) that exact-text specs and locale-paired EN/AR specs assert on
adding a server guard or reordering error precedence on an endpoint that e2e helpers call or refusal specs assert error codes on; removing a navigation control specs drive
preventive_checks: Grep unit tests, MSW handlers, tests/e2e helpers/drivers and specs for the component/endpoint and update them in the same commit
Run the dependent suites (the component's own tests plus every e2e spec that renders it) right after the edit
When a stub goes live, convert fixture-based specs to live-API assertions

Grep e2e specs and drivers for fill() on the field's testid, literal glyphs and the old rendered strings; make specs select non-default branches explicitly; update and run both locale variants of every touched spec
grep the e2e spec directory for callers of the endpoint, its error codes and the removed control's role/testid, and run those specs in the same PR

FS-20.name: Concurrent sessions share one working tree or branch
FS-20.mechanism: Several agent sessions edit, stash, reset, checkout or commit in the same primary checkout or branch. Uncommitted work is destroyed or swept into another session's stash or commit, HEAD moves underneath a session, and partial commits leave the committed tree referencing files that exist only in someone's working directory.
trigger_signals: git status shows dirty files from unrelated feature areas
about to edit, stash, reset or checkout in the primary checkout while other sessions are active
a second agent dispatched into a worktree another agent is still editing
about to push/deploy a branch several sessions committed to
a shared dev box whose checked-out branch and .env other people change; a shared cross-session memory file
cherry-picking or committing on a shared main tree that other live sessions push to; resuming with 'continue' after a gap in a tree the user also operates on
a pathspec commit that fails a different pre-commit hook on unrelated files at each retry; a build failure that names files you never touched
preventive_checks: Work in a dedicated git worktree per session/agent; never bare git stash/reset in a shared directory
Commit small increments immediately, stage explicit paths and diff --cached against the intended list
Before deploying, build/test a fresh clean checkout of the committed HEAD
Delete files only by exact name after checking git status for tracked vs untracked
When a shared box starts erroring mid-task, check its git branch and .env DB target before retrying; re-read shared files immediately before writing

Before every commit or cherry-pick in a shared tree: git fetch, confirm the current branch is the task's, and diff for changes you didn't make; after a concurrent merge grep for duplicate top-level declarations before trusting the Metro bundle
Suspect a concurrent writer (pre-commit stashes unstaged files); check git status for files you didn't touch before trusting a build failure, and move the work to a worktree

FS-21.name: External or untrusted input accepted without bounds, sanitization or isolation
FS-21.mechanism: Client, bot, import or upload input reaches validators, DB columns, parsers and renderers with only happy-path handling: missing numeric/type bounds on JSON, isdigit gates, varchar overflow, one bad unit aborting a batch, over-broad regex/substring matches, heuristics that under-fit real noise, sanitizer bypasses, tar path traversal, ReDoS, verbatim text into agent-parsed documents, permissive security defaults (CORS, no throttle). Malformed input 500s or becomes a vulnerability.
trigger_signals: a serializer/validator accepts nested JSON, id strings, amounts/counts, or bot-writable fields
an import/sync from an external export or API, or a batch loop over many independent units
a regex or substring match over free text, HTML, URLs or transcripts
extracting archives, rendering stored HTML, embedding user text into markdown/LLM input, a new auth endpoint or a new settings default
user-entered or imported dates and quantities that drive ledger posting (payment_date, purchase date, bank statement date, gallons_sold); ids and list items in LLM-authored JSON
a single-item recovery/retry helper with early return reused inside a batch loop (bulk export to device contacts)
a template literal inserts any variable, even a trusted constant, into SQL text
csv.DictReader header keys matched by exact string (lowered but not stripped) in an upload/import validator, and the parser exists in more than one method
a new endpoint or parser taking free-form strings, ids, markdown, uploaded bytes or bot-written JSON, especially when several lanes each add such endpoints
bot/LLM-written JSON with int- or list-typed fields (bool passes isinstance(int)), or a guard that checks only the container type before a destructive step
a large body processed inside a transaction with locks, relying on the global request-size limit
preventive_checks: Parametrize malformed-input tests per field (nested dict/list/bool, negative, oversized, non-ASCII digits) asserting 400, not 500
Isolate each import unit in its own transaction/try and log failures; validate/truncate to column bounds; normalize names before matching
Anchor and bound regexes; scope URL matchers to the external domain and test that own-domain URLs are excluded
Route all HTML through the shared sanitizer, use safe archive extraction, flatten newlines in agent-parsed text, add throttles and an explicit prod CORS allowlist

Add plausible-range date validators and cross-field checks (amount > 0 requires quantity > 0); clip to the minimum width of every column a value propagates into; coerce LLM-supplied ids and guard list item types
Collect per-item results in batch loops and test N>1 where item 1 fails and items 2..N still succeed
Route every dynamic SQL value through a $N placeholder and grep for template-literal SQL in review
Test CSV input with header whitespace, a BOM, case variants and a blank extra column; grep for every sibling copy of the parser and fix them together (FS-62)

Lane 0: build one shared hostile-input fixture set (NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8 and other bad encodings, deep nesting, numeric strings beyond int parse limits, oversize bodies, wrong content types, bool-for-int, unclosed tags and prose < >, structural markdown tokens in titles) plus a parametrized runner; every new endpoint and parser must pass it with 4xx, never 500, before merge
Keep escaping, tag stripping, id coercion and JSON element-shape validation in one shared helper and reuse it; grep sibling lanes for private copies
Cap the body size per endpoint before taking any lock, decode bytes strictly, and validate before the first side effect

FS-22.name: Capability built in one layer but never connected to the next
FS-22.mechanism: One layer implements a capability and the adjacent one never consumes it: PATCH exists but no edit UI, backend search/pagination not exposed, a filter param in the cache key but not the queryset, persisted settings the runtime ignores, audit fields not serialized, a cap computed but not enforced, a label prop never supplied, a specialized mutation imported but unused behind a silently succeeding fallback. Each layer's tests pass.
trigger_signals: the backend accepts params or returns fields the FE component doesn't read or render
a spec item is a cap, breaker, limit or setting whose enforcement lives in another code path
a prop/arg/param is threaded through types but its source or sink isn't in the diff
an unused hook/mutation import, or a control labeled as a toggle with no handler
a field drives sorting or overdue logic in a selector but has zero JSX usages
preventive_checks: For every accepted param or setting, test that the output actually changes when it is supplied
Trace each new field DB -> serializer -> FE render (and back for edits) as one checklist
Test the enforcement branch of any cap/breaker/guard, not only the computation
Add a render test asserting that the formatted value of every new sort/business field appears on the card

FS-23.name: Shared identifier changed or claimed without enumerating its users
FS-23.mechanism: A name or contract used across the codebase (route path, testid, barrel export, codename, query-param key, RTK endpoint name, function signature, row-dict schema, global client config, shared primitive default) is renamed, extended or newly claimed, and only the obvious consumers are updated. Hardcoded strings in other components, tests, exporters, nginx or parallel workstreams keep the old meaning or collide.
trigger_signals: renaming a route, testid, export, codename or label
adding a query-param key, RTK endpoint name or URL path in a shared namespace (router, nginx, apiSlice)
adding a parameter or field to a function/row dict consumed elsewhere; changing a shared primitive or global client default for one feature

a form-state path or local name reused for a second meaning (row id field, handler param shadowing a prop); a new package named like an existing module; a changed sentinel value; a list repointed to a new entity
an infra migration stops or replaces a VM, zone or IP that deploy/ops scripts reference by name
an e2e driver references a testid string with zero matches in src/; a copy/label rename done only in message catalogs
a shared pure helper's return shape changes (one array split into two) while a parallel branch also consumes it, and git reports no conflict
preventive_checks: Grep the whole repo (src, tests/e2e, helpers, docs, nginx conf) for the old and new identifier before and after the change
Reference routes and codenames through shared constants and add a registry-vs-usage contract test
Change shared primitives via a new variant/prop rather than the default
Run the real build (npm run build) after any rename
Grep the whole repo (deploy/, scripts/, docs) for old instance names, zones and IPs in the migration change and smoke-run the deploy right after
Add a check that fails on driver/spec testid strings with no match in application source; grep e2e/ for the literal old copy, not only messages/*.json
Before merging a helper contract change, grep every call site across open branches and add a characterization test per consumer

FS-24.name: Pushed, merged or deployed state assumed instead of checked
FS-24.mechanism: Work is reported merged, deployed or live because it was pushed, because automation (auto-PR/automerge, deploy-on-merge) usually fires, or because memory says so. The automation silently didn't run (branch already existed, Actions budget exhausted), the fix sits unmerged in a worktree, or only staging got it while the verifier checks prod.
trigger_signals: about to tell the user 'merged', 'deployed', 'live' or 'shipped'
pushed a claude/* branch expecting automerge, or merged to staging expecting auto-deploy
memory or a prior session claims a fix already landed
the instruction says 'deploy' but no deploy command for that environment is known
a revert on one branch while the fix already promoted elsewhere; a branch prefix vs the workflow trigger glob; a merged fix not live because an unrelated broken build blocks deploy
preventive_checks: Verify with git ls-remote / gh pr list / gh run list for the exact SHA and confirm origin/<base> contains the commit
Check the deployed artifact on the exact domain the verifier uses (asset hash, endpoint response)
State git, PR and deploy status explicitly in every done report ('pushed only' when that is the truth)
Read .github/workflows before assuming automation behavior
Run git branch -r --contains <sha> on every promoted branch; check the environment's CI build history and the deploy system's deployment log, not process uptime

FS-25.name: Errors swallowed, conflated or silently defaulted
FS-25.mechanism: Error handling collapses distinct failure classes or hides them: 4xx treated like transient 5xx, a generic isError triggering logout, config errors surfacing as 500, IntegrityError instead of 400, only top-level detail read so field errors vanish, fire-and-forget mutations dropping 400s, silent fallbacks (resolver defaults, a ?? b, dev mock on any error, 'non-fatal' config set). The UI or report looks fine while the real failure disappears. On mobile a boot gate's .catch only logs, so its readiness flag is never set and the app freezes on the splash, and an idempotent 'already applied' response arrives on the same rejected branch as a real failure.
trigger_signals: try/except or catch around external calls or mutations with a single broad fallback
code branches on isError/non-2xx without inspecting the status or error code
a form or toast shows one generic message; a mutation called without await/catch
a ?? / or-default / fallback-to-fixture on a value that is persisted or user-visible
a retry loop around an unrecoverable input; a CI cache miss that silently falls back to a slow full build; try/except around ledger posting in save()

a readiness flag set only inside .then() with a .catch that only logs; an async redeem/apply action with more than one success-like outcome; an env-prefix resolver that returns None when its env var is missing; an email/SMS send wrapped in log-and-continue
a catch block issues ROLLBACK or other cleanup before rethrowing
preventive_checks: Test a mocked 400 with field errors and assert the field message renders; test the shared error helper against every DRF body shape
Surface 4xx distinctly from 5xx/timeouts and map domain/config exceptions to explicit statuses in the same PR
Await persisting mutations, revert optimistic state and toast on rejection
Make resolvers/fallbacks raise under test, and read config back after setting it

Force init to reject in a test and assert the UI reaches an error/retry state; enumerate backend response codes and map each to a UI outcome; make config resolvers raise at boot on missing inputs; alert, not only log, on provider auth/4xx failures
Wrap cleanup inside error handlers in its own try/catch, log its failure, and always rethrow the original error

FS-26.name: Boundary values and NULL/join semantics not exercised
FS-26.mechanism: Logic is written for typical values and misses empty, zero, single-option, null or absent keys, falsy-but-valid values, timezone shifts, clamps and cap-plus-suffix limits, overlapping conditions, and SQL/ORM semantics such as NULL under exclude(), order_by leaking into GROUP BY, and joins double-counting rows. Fixtures never contain the degenerate case.
trigger_signals: exclude(field=value) or a filter on a nullable/JSON key; values().annotate() on an already-ordered queryset
a dict built from query rows then indexed by every possible key; sums over rows reachable through several joins
if value: on fields where 0/''/[] are valid; Number()/int() on parsed string segments
a picker that can have exactly one option, date math mixing local and UTC, a permission matrix with 3+ combinations

fixtures never contain a NULL, zero, negative, net-zero or sentinel row: a nullable boolean filtered with field=False, a nullable FK dereferenced on legacy data, zero-item entities, a sentinel shared by many rows, an as-of date for a cumulative figure
a feed selector maps over child rows (steps) that share a parent (contact); a 'set once, applies broadly' value (reminder due date) stored on one child row
tiered rates (day/week/month) priced as the finest tier times a count
`if e.response:` / `if resp:` on a requests.Response (falsy for any status >= 400) inside an error handler or log statement (recurs even though 'is not None' is listed below)
value-based redaction or replace-by-value over a bundle that can hold very short values (1-3 characters)
preventive_checks: Add explicit tests for empty, zero, one, null/absent, max-length and cross-timezone inputs
Use isnull filters for absent JSON keys, clear order_by before aggregating, and dedupe by id across many-to-many joins
Replace truthiness checks with 'is not None' and validate formats with a strict regex before coercion
Enumerate every combination of multi-flag conditions and route modes in a table-driven test

Use exclude(field=True) for nullable booleans; test legacy rows with null FKs and all-empty collections; build report skeletons from the union of per-period rows; compute cumulative adjustments as of the entry's own date
Test a parent with N>1 children: exactly one card, and the value survives completing the first child
Write table-driven tests at every tier boundary (7 and 30 days, remainders) against the published rate card
Add a test that a 4xx error path logs the provider's real response body
Redact by secret-marked key with a minimum value length, and test with a 1-character value

FS-27.name: Existing primitive or house pattern bypassed
FS-27.mechanism: New code hand-rolls something the codebase already provides or mandates: the shared form and form-field components, searchable select and async-select pickers, dnd-kit, the shared modal's props, the global error-toast opt-out, the shared hours formatter, the shared KPI tile, the preferences store, the outbox for external I/O, the settings config helper, the e2e driver location, an existing WebSocket bridge. It works in isolation but reintroduces solved bugs and inconsistency, and is flagged in review.
trigger_signals: adding a form, picker, drag interaction, modal, stat row, settings card or displayed number
new external I/O, settings block, per-user toggle storage or realtime delivery
creating an e2e driver/helper, or a component file in a feature that has a barrel
writing a new management command/script for a data check; a new model or report layout next to an established precedent
writing a fresh store upload/release script (Play Publisher, ASC API) while one already exists in the repo's scripts/
a design system that offers both a native-popup Select and a fully custom popup, used for a fixed enum whose design shows a styled panel
a new GitHub Actions workflow that pushes or opens PRs; a new true-negative fixture in a set whose siblings follow an unvalidated convention
preventive_checks: Search the shared UI and shared utility modules, sibling features and the project's agent conventions file (CLAUDE.md) for an existing primitive before writing a new one
Copy the pattern from the nearest sibling usage and route numbers through the shared formatter
Add barrel exports and driver methods in the same commit as the new file
