Reuse and extend the committed release scripts instead of hand-rolling API calls
Open the popup when pixel-matching and use the fully custom popup component for fixed enums
Copy the permissions: block and PR-creation action from sibling workflows; match the non-obvious fields of sibling fixtures, not only the literal expected value

FS-29.name: Code assumes the host environment it was written on
FS-29.mechanism: Code or config depends on properties of the author's environment: 127.0.0.1 across Docker network namespaces, Docker DNS aliases after going native, localhost resolving to IPv6, PATH in a login shell vs systemd, macOS Python without certifi, GNU vs BSD tools, DB superuser privileges, localhost defaults for absolute URLs, CORS pinned to the default port, unpinned CDN versions, stale topology runbooks. It works locally and fails where it actually runs.
trigger_signals: a service addressed via 127.0.0.1/localhost/host.docker.internal, or a new base-URL setting with a localhost default
a daemon shells out to a CLI; a script run on macOS vs Linux; a new tool in a deploy step
moving a service between Docker and native, or booting on a non-default port
a CDN script without a pinned version; a runbook/memory describing infra topology

settings that unconditionally fetch Secrets Manager credentials or define remote DB aliases; a local credential override that can activate in prod; optional binaries/packages (soffice, PyMuPDF) in a fresh sandbox
a background or non-interactive shell runs python3/node by name; a verification script on a VM calls the VM's own public hostname; a saved SSH/infra connection recipe from an earlier session
a deploy config reuses an app's default dev ports on a VM that already hosts another app; a relative sqlite path in DATABASE_URL copied into a worktree's .env
an e2e or preview server falls back to an alternate port because the default is taken
a stdlib urllib client on a python.org macOS build; writing an absolute machine path into a committed settings file; staging a restore file for a service account under a mode-700 home or tmp dir

a skill or pipeline helper imports an optional module (fitz/PyMuPDF, numpy, pyzbar) or shells out to a renderer chain (pdftoppm, mutool, magick/convert) or a native lib (zbar), and runs in a fresh per-run sandbox or parallel benchmark worktree (recurs: every parallel sandbox rediscovers the same missing module on its first action even though this trigger was listed)
building a redirect Location or absolute URL from the request path/host in an app served behind a reverse proxy with a path prefix
new syntax or stdlib API (backslashes or reused quotes inside f-string expressions, match, newer typing features) in code that also runs on hosts with an older supported interpreter
preventive_checks: Verify reachability from inside the real runtime (curl from the container or systemd unit), not from your shell
Use 127.0.0.1 vs ::1 consistently between client and server, and derive allowed origins from config rather than the default port
Check command -v, the platform and DB role privileges before relying on them; use requests/certifi in scripts
Pin dependency versions and re-check topology (systemctl status / docker ps) once per session before trusting a runbook
Provide a settings_localtest module for offline tests, gate credential overrides by environment, and pre-flight or fall back for optional dependencies

Pin absolute interpreter paths in background scripts; verify public endpoints from a different host (clouds don't hairpin NAT); probe saved hosts cheaply before use and update memory in the same change as any infra migration
Enumerate bound ports on the target (ss -ltnp) and treat ports as deploy inputs; use absolute sqlite paths in DATABASE_URL
In non-prod allow every port e2e/dev servers may pick in CORS_ORIGIN, or reserve and document one fixed e2e port

Check a file's git tracked-ness before writing machine-specific values and use the .local override; stage files for a service account with install -o <svc> and check sudo -u <svc> test -r <path> first

Probe the sandbox once before the first step that needs it (python -c 'import fitz, numpy'; command -v pdftoppm mutool magick; decode a trivial barcode image to prove the zbar dylib loads), record the working choice, and route every later call to it

Make helpers import optional dependencies inside try/except and fall straight through to the next working renderer or a Pillow/stdlib-only path, and bake native libs (poppler, zbar) into the sandbox image instead of installing them mid-task
Build public URLs from a configured public base URL (or trusted forwarded headers) and curl the public host to assert the Location header before go-live
Set the linter/compiler target to the minimum supported runtime (ruff target-version, tsconfig target) and compile or run the tests under that floor interpreter in CI

FS-30.name: Working from a stale base or without checking existing work
FS-30.mechanism: A branch, worktree or audit runs against a snapshot that has fallen behind a fast-moving shared branch, or starts without checking whether the work already exists or is in flight. Overlapping edits, duplicate implementations and audits graded against the wrong code surface only at merge or review.
trigger_signals: starting work on a ticket key or a hot shared file while other sessions are active
a branch/worktree older than a few hours on a trunk receiving large refactors
launching an audit/gap-analysis agent mid-session while others push
consolidating via cherry-pick/rebase followed by push
dispatching isolation:worktree agents right after committing on the orchestrator's branch; a cherry-pick conflict on a large, frequently edited file
a new spec asserts a field's required/optional state while another merged ticket also touched that field
preventive_checks: Before starting: git fetch; git log origin/staging --grep <ticket>; gh pr list --search <ticket>
Diff touched files against current origin/staging before substantive work and again before merge; cherry-pick feature commits onto the fresh tip
Audit agents fetch first and log the origin SHA they graded; anchor every agent to its assigned worktree path
Gate push on a clean rebase exit and a full build after consolidation

Pin each worktree agent's base to an explicit branch/SHA and check it with git merge-base --is-ancestor before trusting its report; resolve hot-file conflicts with a 3-way merge (git merge-file), never --theirs/--ours, then grep for known recent fixes
Read the field's current validation in the latest shipped code and requirement before asserting it
After any scripted per-hunk ours/theirs resolution run eslint and tsc on every resolved file; prefer whole-file theirs for rewritten specs

FS-31.name: Cache identity or invalidation misses a dependency
FS-31.mechanism: A cached value depends on more inputs than its key or tags express: RTK mutations invalidate only their own tag while list, summary or version views also show the field, optimistic patches skip server-computed fields, differing arg shapes defeat dedup, and backend cache keys omit view kind, pagination independence, None-vs-empty, or database identity (one Redis shared by several worktree DBs). Stale or cross-contaminated data appears only after the right sequence.
trigger_signals: a new mutation or query endpoint in a domain with existing cached views, or 'copy the invalidation list from X'
a mutation with server-side effects on fields other than the one sent
introducing a backend cache, or adding pagination/filters to a cached endpoint
several databases (dev/e2e/worktrees) sharing one Redis with id-only keys
a CI schema-snapshot or build cache shared across branches whose migration graphs diverge
a per-run DB dropped and recreated under the same name while a cache namespace is keyed by DB name and row ids
preventive_checks: List every field the mutation changes and every cached view that shows it; add each to invalidatesTags and test by reading the view after the mutation
Reconcile the full mutation response into caches instead of hand-patching one field
Include every value-shaping dimension in backend cache keys (view kind, filters, DB/env namespace) and test that two variants don't collide
Reuse existing hook argument shapes so RTK Query can dedupe
Key snapshot restores by an exact migration-set hash and branch, and purge the whole prefix (not one key) when poisoned
Flush the DB's cache namespace immediately after every CREATE DATABASE in pool/shard scripts and test two consecutive runs that create the same ids

FS-32.name: Side effects not ordered against the commit or outcome they depend on
FS-32.mechanism: Notifications, cache invalidation, external calls, ledger rows and 'added' reports fire before validation/commit or are recorded from intent instead of the confirmed result: cache.delete inside atomic, notify before a later field is validated, a guard appended after side effects, a local record deleted before the remote revoke is confirmed, outbox ops without enforced dependencies, failure counters rolled back with the raise. Success paths look right; rollback and partial-failure paths leak.
trigger_signals: a multi-step create/transition/share method that emits notifications, webhooks or external I/O
cache invalidation or a signal handler next to a DB write inside transaction.atomic
an outbox/queue op that needs another op's result (depends_on) or is enqueued inside a loop
bookkeeping (ledger, result set, local credential record) written next to a call that can fail or no-op
preventive_checks: Validate all inputs before any side effect, and fire notifications and cache invalidation via transaction.on_commit
Record outcomes from what the apply call confirmed per item, not from the precomputed diff
Enforce op dependencies at the single shared dispatch entry point; test dependent + dependency enqueued together and exact enqueue counts
Test the failure path: counters persist across a raised exception and nothing is notified when validation fails

FS-33.name: Test double or harness silently diverges from the real runtime
FS-33.mechanism: Mocks, fakes and harness setup are more permissive than, or never intercept, the real dependency: stateful MSW handlers without the backend's scoping and rules, a fake CLI without reserved-name validation, monkeypatching a queryset method the code doesn't call, bespoke render wrappers missing providers, jsdom clipboard/userEvent ordering, caplog on propagate=False loggers, Playwright '*' globs that don't cross '/', destructured request methods, missing xfail markers. Tests go green without exercising reality.
trigger_signals: writing a stateful mock handler or a fake for a backend/CLI that has business rules
mocking one method (filter) where the code may call another (select_for_update)
a custom render wrapper, clipboard mock, caplog assertion or page.route glob
a docstring claims tests are xfail/expected-fail
a concurrency test with threads inside django TestCase; near-duplicate Gherkin steps bound to mock vs live implementations
a fake collaborator returns a fixed correct value where the real one derives it from input; a harness copies the repo with blanket excludes (.git)
preventive_checks: Derive mock rules from the backend service (scope by route params, same allowed transitions), one test per rule
Assert the mock/route handler was actually hit; use /** globs and call request.method()
Use the shared renderWithProviders, check logger propagate settings before caplog, and call userEvent.setup() before defining clipboard mocks
Revert the fix and confirm the test fails
Make fakes reproduce the real input-dependent behavior; grep the suite for reliance on excluded dirs (git rev-parse) and compare harness pass counts with a full checkout

FS-34.name: Nondeterministic test timing and ordering
FS-34.mechanism: Tests race the app or each other: waitForResponse registered after goto, reload before the mutation response lands, smooth scroll vs actionability, skeleton assertions against same-tick stubs, hover/drag under parallel workers, headless dnd coordinates, real clock vs fixed fixture dates, order-dependent DB or polyfill leakage between tests. Failures move between runs and get misread as regressions.
trigger_signals: a spec triggers a navigation/mutation and then waits for its network response
drag/hover interaction specs in a suite with parallel workers
date-specific fixtures without page.clock, or loading-state assertions against stubs
a different single test fails each full run but every file passes alone

a date-picker spec clicks a testid embedding a literal ISO date; a transition-class assertion right after a navigation that remounts the wrapper; Escape sent right after opening a dialog whose handler is dialog-scoped
a driver closes a Radix menu/popover/dialog and immediately clicks another trigger, types, or sends Escape while the closing overlay is still mounted for its exit animation or returning focus

changing the runtime under an e2e suite (Vite dev -> production build, cold vs warm dev server, more workers, faster backend): specs that sampled an intermediate state or used a fixed 10 s expect timeout were calibrated to the old speed
a driver that moves a ProseMirror/BlockNote caret and presses a key as soon as the DOM selection moves; UI state hydrated from a server preference that a spec toggles and reloads
an e2e step clicks outside a Radix/headless overlay right after opening it (outside-pointer listeners are armed a tick after open)
a query-count test compares two requests on a fresh connection while the app has per-connection probes or process-level caches; a test that passes in the full run but fails alone
preventive_checks: Register waitForResponse before the triggering action and await mutations before any reload
Pin page.clock for date fixtures; run drag/hover specs serially and prove the logic with a unit test
Rerun suspects standalone twice and treat 'different failure each run' as isolation leakage (polyfills, DB cleanup)

Compute dates relative to a pinned page.clock and page the calendar to the target month; poll for the incoming node (route-scoped id or last()) across remounts; wait for focus inside the dialog before sending dialog-scoped keys

Every driver close helper waits for the overlay (role=menu/dialog, radix popper wrapper) to detach and focus-return to finish before the next interaction; never click a trigger while another overlay is mounted

Before switching runtime or worker width, grep specs for networkidle, toHaveURL on intermediate routes and fixed sleeps, assert only final settled state (a route-ready testid), warm the dev server before the setup project, and require 3 green runs at the new width with an isolated control

Poll the editor's own state (view.state.selection) and wait on the concrete GET/PUT of server-hydrated preferences before the next key or reload; run every touched spec with --repeat-each=3 before commit
Wait for the overlay's open state and a frame before the outside click, or poll for dismissal; prove with --repeat-each 4
Make one untimed warm-up request with the same URL shape on the same data before counting, and run every new test alone in a fresh process as well as in the parallel full run

FS-35.name: Test depends on uncontrolled shared data or unrealistic setup
FS-35.mechanism: Specs and fixtures lean on persisted shared e2e data or on setup that doesn't match production: seeded workspaces archived by other specs, per-user preferences shared across specs, rows accumulating across runs, DBs reused across branches, a real browser profile leaking in, actors without memberships, filter values that don't isolate the case, destructive steps that hit invariant guards. Results depend on run history, not on the code.
trigger_signals: a spec mutates or depends on a shared seeded workspace/project/board instead of creating its own
a seed helper with fixed dates/names on a DB that persists across runs or branches
a global per-user preference written by one spec and read by others
a test actor created ad hoc without membership/role, or an app launched without a fresh profile
an e2e spec or seed script inserts rows by direct DB access with no teardown or prune step; a re-runnable seed that only issues INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

a negative/absence fixture names a real entity (subdomain, vendor) that ongoing work is onboarding; seeding a 'connected' flag that gates a live external API call; a browser session carried across dev-server restarts or earlier OAuth attempts

an exact count asserted on a shared scratch/seed project; a spec that creates its own project but still references the shared seed project id; a seed helper that silently no-ops when the board already has data
a narrowing search term built from short numeric or common tokens against word-split backend search; extra browser contexts created while the config sets use.storageState
re-running a pipeline or lab run (document ingest, import) into the same project or tenant that still holds an earlier run's output
preventive_checks: Create throwaway entities per spec through API/seed helpers and clean up in try/finally
Use unique generated values for constrained fields, and recreate the e2e DB when switching worktrees/branches
Compute expected results from the seed data inside the test, and give test actors real memberships
Reset persisted preferences and pass a fresh userDataDir per launch
Tag every e2e-created row with a fixed marker (prefix or is_test flag) at creation, delete by exact match in teardown, and assert row counts stay stable across two consecutive runs
Make seeds converge: remove rows outside the intended set before inserting, and test by injecting a drifted row and re-seeding

Use synthetic reserved values for 'not yet supported' fixtures; default seeded integration flags to the disconnected state; pin SECRET_KEY in the local env and use a fresh browser context after restarts or earlier auth flows
Create a throwaway project per spec for exact-count or config-writing assertions and grep specs for writes on shared seed ids

Use unique alphanumeric tokens that cannot appear in keys or timestamps; create extra-user contexts with an explicit empty storageState and pass the user's own workspace slug, asserting the signed-in user first
Test seed commands by running them twice and asserting row counts unchanged
Create a fresh project per run, or assert the target is empty before starting, and compare the result against the run's own inputs

FS-36.name: Ambiguous or constraint-bearing ask resolved without asking
FS-36.mechanism: An instruction admits more than one reasonable model (which surface or component, per-project vs central roles, deployment-wide vs per-tenant keys, which of several workspaces named after the product, inline vs listed attachments) or collides with an earlier decision or constraint (a rejected design, a unique(kind) constraint, RBAC on the guarded field), and the agent silently picks the convenient reading and builds a lot on it.
trigger_signals: the request names a generic surface/component that maps to several implementations
two standard data-ownership models both fit the wording
the instruction contradicts a documented rejected approach or an existing uniqueness/permission constraint
an irreversible bulk write targeted by an informal name, or 'copy the front end from repo Y'
an ambiguous domain term that already names a distinct feature; the orchestration/visibility model for a multi-hour fan-out
choosing the sort direction/tiebreaker for a to-do-like feed; a complaint that a prefilled field 'shouldn't be editable'

building backend endpoints for a design-parity feature before the frames are available; replacing a free-text field with a fixed-enum picker; a list's primary decision (accept/reject) reachable only from a details modal
preventive_checks: State the chosen interpretation and the alternatives in one line and ask before building, or ship one small representative slice first
Re-read earlier rejections/ADRs and the constraints of the model the feature layers onto; spike the blocking assumption
Confirm the exact target (id, domain) before irreversible writes
Ask whether a prefilled scaffold value should stay locked or disappear; confirm FIFO vs newest-first for task lists and write the ordering test first
Keep the API shape provisional until frames are captured; ask whether the value space is really closed (offer Other plus free text); ask whether the primary decision must be a row action

FS-37.name: Authorization decided on a proxy instead of the real identity or entitlement
FS-37.mechanism: Access checks rely on something that correlates with the right answer but isn't it: a stored foreign id instead of current membership, single-use codes not bound to the requester, display names/trigger words or comment text instead of the authenticated author, unverified email for cross-system identity, codenames shared by bots and humans, RLS bound to workspace instead of viewer, null === null while auth loads, exact row ownership instead of the tenancy boundary, manage granted without its view prerequisite.
trigger_signals: minting a credential/session or redeeming a code; matching identities across systems
a gate for a human action on an endpoint also reachable by bots/service accounts
a trust signal derived from content patterns or display fields
a permission comparison using optional chaining, an RLS policy on a membership table, or a backfill granting codenames
a permission pre-flight classifies a write (fields changed, create vs update, delete) separately from the upsert that performs it; a test-only endpoint gated by a docstring
a new service/machine-identity auth path reuses a TTL-cached user-state helper built for login sessions
preventive_checks: Test the negative actor explicitly: revoked member, bot token, another session's cookie, unverified email, auth still loading
Give non-human actors dedicated least-privilege roles and exclude them from human pickers and approval gates
Resolve senders by tenant-scoped secret and authors by authenticated identity, never by text or display values
Grant view prerequisites alongside manage codenames and test the role end to end

Derive the classification from the same DB lookup and field set the writer uses, keep the check inside the shared write helper, and test fabricated ids, uncompared fields and content swaps; gate test-only endpoints at runtime
Check high-privilege service tokens against fresh state per request (or invalidate on deactivation) and test that deactivating the account makes the very next request 401

FS-38.name: Soft-deleted and terminal-state rows ignored by constraints and queries
FS-38.mechanism: Rows in deleted, archived or rejected states still participate in unique constraints, joins and aggregates, or their dependents are not cascaded: re-create after soft delete 500s on the unique constraint, Count() through relations bypasses the soft-delete manager, dedupe keeps a phantom row, SET_NULL parents un-hide children, deleting a bot leaves its membership seat, cascade restore via all_objects conflates batches. The default soft-delete manager hides only the queried model's own deleted rows, so rows under a soft-deleted PARENT still leak into counts, scoping helpers and eligibility checks.
trigger_signals: the model uses SoftDeleteModel and has a unique/unique_together constraint or natural key
an aggregate, annotation or join reaches a soft-deletable model
deleting an entity that owns related rows (membership, synthetic user, children)
a constraint meant as 'one active X' written as 'one X ever'
a get-or-restore or create path that revives a soft-deleted row a merge deliberately removed; callbacks that can write to a terminal-state task
a serializer inlines a Prefetch of a soft-deletable model in a payload that an offline-sync pull persists to devices
a scoping helper, count, aggregate, retry-eligibility check or service method that reaches a row whose PARENT (project, document, page, ticket) is soft-deletable
a tenancy resolver or helper that uses all_objects, or a service that accepts model instances resolved by another caller (bot approve path)
a decision/resolution workflow whose every option dereferences user-deletable content, or a new dependent table under an existing unlink/delete path
an automated handoff or reassignment to a stored person (reporter, owner, creator) who may have left the workspace since
preventive_checks: Test soft-delete then re-create with the same key; look up all_objects by natural key and revive before create
Add filter=Q(is_deleted=False) to aggregates and compare list vs detail counts
Use conditional unique constraints scoped to active status; cascade soft-delete to children with a batch id
Test deleting the parent and assert dependent rows/seats are released
Check the merge log and deletion reason before reviving; reject writes to terminal states
Filter deleted_at in every Prefetch/inline queryset of a soft-deletable model and add a sync test that a soft-deleted child disappears on the other device

Lane 0: write a parent-chain table of every entity and its soft-deletable ancestors (e.g. project -> document -> page -> section; project -> ticket -> link) with the filter each query and aggregate must add (page__is_deleted=False, project__deleted_at__isnull=True); every brief cites it

Test every aggregate, scoping helper and eligibility check with a soft-deleted PARENT (not only a soft-deleted row) and assert exclusion; services re-check liveness of passed instances and their ancestors
Give every decision that dereferences deletable content a fallback resolution, and extend the existing delete/unlink path whenever a dependent table is added
Test each automated assignment with a departed member and decide the fallback (skip, reassign, escalate) instead of letting a validation error roll the transition back

FS-39.name: Parallel agents dispatched onto overlapping files or allocators
FS-39.mechanism: Work fans out to parallel agents/branches whose scopes overlap on one app's migrations, sequence numbers, shared helpers, components or singleton rows, or forks from a tip missing a sibling's finished work. Each branch is green alone; the merged tree has conflicting migrations, duplicate abstractions, IntegrityErrors, or specs asserting the other branch's placeholder.
trigger_signals: about to dispatch parallel worktree agents that touch the same Django app, shared service file or component
each branch will add a migration or claim the next sequence number
a phase forked before its sibling phase merged, or a docs/wrap-up task running concurrently with implementers
a forked/resumed session says background agents died
parallel feature branches (not only agents) each add a migration off the same parent before landing on a shared stage branch
parallel branches bump one global client schema constant (SQLite SCHEMA_VERSION) or add the next Django migration number

a merge or conflict resolution inside a brace-structured file (CSS, JSON message bundle, TS API client), including one git reports as conflict-free; a long-lived or batch of feature branches merged into main that each touched models.py
parallel worktree tickets that each bump one global version constant (EXTRACTOR_VERSION)
parallel lanes each adding error codes, fields or enums to one shared contract module that the FE mirrors by hand
an integration branch receiving lane merges while the base branch keeps moving; lanes deviating from a shared written spec
preventive_checks: Partition by file ownership; pre-assign shared helper names/owners and migration numbers, or plan a makemigrations --merge step
Re-check the app's latest migration number against origin/staging immediately before merge
Fork dependent phases from the merged tip and run docs/wrap-up last
Re-run every touched spec on the fully merged tree before declaring the gate green; confirm the original coordinator is dead before relaunching
Run makemigrations --check on the shared branch right after each merge and commit any merge migration a task depends on
Before merging, read the target's current SCHEMA_VERSION / latest migration and take the next free number; treat every merge touching the constant as a conflict-check step

After every merge, JSON-parse touched bundles, run the typecheck and the production build, and run makemigrations --check / showmigrations for every app with migrations before commit or deploy; resolve mid-object conflicts by re-inserting the added block into one side, never by concatenating both
Reserve the next version value centrally before dispatch or serialize those tickets
Lane 0: generate FE client types from the API schema, or add a code/field parity test, before lanes start adding to the contract
Merge the base branch into the integration branch every wave and re-run every lane's scoped tests on the merged tree; record spec deviations in the spec as they happen

FS-40.name: Invariant enforced in app code without a lock or DB constraint
FS-40.mechanism: Uniqueness, single-row, idempotency and state-transition invariants are enforced by check-then-act in Python (exists() then insert, delete+create, get_or_create/get on non-unique fields, time-window undo, whole-instance save()) without select_for_update, a DB constraint or update_fields. Serial tests pass; concurrent requests, retries, multiple workers or dirty shared DBs break the invariant. In multi-lane builds the lock order is assembled per lane and the harness checks only the first acquisition per kind, so hidden locks (FK KEY SHARE on a FOR UPDATE parent, unique-insert waits, late DELETEs, counter rows, helper-internal locks, re-locks of an earlier tier) deadlock, and each local deadlock fix introduces the next.
trigger_signals: an exists()/get() check followed by an insert, especially with external I/O in between
a worker/outbox table polled by more than one process, or a retryable create-then-persist
save() on a model whose other fields are written asynchronously
get_or_create or .get() on fields with no UniqueConstraint; new automatic assignment of a relation
update_or_create/get_or_create keyed on one FK shared by two source types; an M2M modelling a single-owner relation; a timeout/reaper that mutates status after killing work
a plan where several lanes add locked write paths to one subsystem, or a fix that adds a lock on an earlier-tier resource late in a transaction

a transaction that also takes hidden locks: FK KEY SHARE checks against a parent held FOR UPDATE, unique-key INSERT waits, DELETE row locks late in the transaction, counter/sequence rows (max+1), row locks inside settle/refresh helpers, advisory locks, a re-lock of an earlier tier after a deeper one
a threaded race/deadlock test with barrier or event park points, or a race test that asserts only 'no exception'
a deadlock fix, or a lock-harness finding answered by broadening lock scope; rows read before the lock is held and written back after
preventive_checks: Back the invariant with a DB constraint and catch IntegrityError to return 400 or an idempotent 200
Use select_for_update (skip_locked for workers) on the anchor row and save(update_fields=[...])
Write a two-concurrent-request or kill-between-steps test, and run seeds twice

Lane 0, before parallel lanes start: enumerate EVERY lockable resource of the subsystem (explicit row locks, FK KEY SHARE checks on locked parents, unique-key insert waits, DELETE row locks, counter/sequence rows, locks inside helper functions, advisory locks) into one global order table that every brief cites

Build the lock-order harness once in lane 0: it records EVERY acquisition, not just the first per kind, flags any re-lock of an earlier tier after a deeper one, and runs inside every lane's scoped tests

Ship a threaded deadlock/race test template in lane 0: two real threads (TransactionTestCase), park point placed BEFORE the lock under test, assert end-state consistency (no lost update, no stranded row), and confirm it fails with the lock removed

Run every deadlock fix back through the harness and the threaded tests for EVERY entry point of the subsystem; in this codebase, fixes that reordered one pair or broadened lock scope introduced new deadlocks
Read the rows you will write only after the lock is held; allocate per-parent sequences under a locked counter row or retry on IntegrityError

FS-41.name: Client derives answers from one page of a paginated list
FS-41.mechanism: The FE filters, sorts, groups, counts, slices or resolves labels over whatever rows it happens to have fetched (one page, .results only) instead of asking the backend. Correct on seed data that fits one page; silently wrong once real data spans pages.
trigger_signals: a search box or group/sort option whose query hook has no matching backend param
.filter/.sort/.slice/.find applied to query results, or a KPI computed from the list held in state
a label resolved by looking up an id in another cached list, or a :key route resolved via fuzzy search results[0]
response.results consumed without count/next
an audit of 'all affected items' built from one page of a CLI/API listing
a list that combines multi-select or an empty state with infinite-scroll appends
preventive_checks: Grep new list code for .filter(/.sort(/.slice( on API results and send search/sort/group as query params
Denormalize display fields (key/title) onto the serializer and add exact-match lookups
Back KPIs with server aggregates and run the e2e with more rows than one page
Reconcile before/after totals exactly when auditing via a paged listing
e2e: select rows, scroll to append the next page, and assert selection count and empty-state text stay correct

FS-42.name: Third-party system semantics not honored
FS-42.mechanism: Integrations wrap an external API or platform using the obvious happy-path semantics: single-page list calls, .json() on a 204, a whole status code treated as idempotent, unguarded None returns, full GET/PUT to flip one flag, unverified trigger/delivery conditions, unknown network reachability, auth-method invariants. Mocks mirror the assumption, so it fails only against the real service.
trigger_signals: a new client method for a third-party list/create/update endpoint
a webhook/bot integration with delivery or trigger conditions, or a push to a service whose host is unstated
provisioning accounts or changing auth methods in an external system
uploading a large binary (AAB/IPA over ~50MB) through googleapiclient/httplib2

a poll/settle parser or error reader written from a vendor integration guide; a webhook-only payment rail (bank wire, virtual IBAN) handled with the redirect rail's correlation key; synthetic identifiers generated for a provider field
a Play Publisher edits.commit or App Store Connect reviewSubmissions call scripted for the first time, or for an app's first-ever submission
an integration needs two same-vendor credential types (GitHub OAuth App vs GitHub App); pinning an input on a third-party CI action to remove its network call

a cluster bootstrapped with a placeholder pull secret, followed by an in-cluster build (BuildConfig / oc start-build), dynamic PVC provisioning, or any platform pod restart after a DiskPressure image GC
preventive_checks: Read the provider docs for pagination, empty bodies, error ids, partial-update endpoints and trigger conditions, and write them down
Contract-test with recorded real responses: 204/empty body, page 2, the specific error body, None
Confirm network direction and reachability before choosing push vs dial-out
Use a chunked resumable MediaFileUpload with a timeout of at least 600s and http.follow_redirects = False, and test with a real full-size artifact

Hit the live/sandbox endpoint once and assert the real payload shape and error-key casing; write the webhook test from a notification payload that carries no internal payment id; generate synthetic ids to the provider's documented format and test that format

Submit an app's first-ever version through the store console (it names the real blocking field); retry a Play commit once with changesNotSentForReview toggled on the 400 naming it, and log which branch ran

Name each credential type by exact product, settings URL and the capability it serves before asking the user; read the action's action.yml/entrypoint to confirm which code path an input actually skips

On a placeholder-secret cluster treat every platform feature whose images come from the authenticated registry as untested: check builder/CSI image registries first, plan an external build (podman) and static/hostPath volumes up front, and after any DiskPressure or eviction event confirm CSI, registry and ingress pods are Running before relying on them

FS-44.name: Migration unsafe for code or data already in the shared DB
FS-44.mechanism: A migration is right for the new code but not for what already exists: NOT NULL columns without db_default applied to a DB shared with older deployed code or parallel agents, constraints older code violates, role/RLS DDL needing privileges the app user lacks, raw SQL without cross-app dependencies, behavior flips with no backfill for existing rows.
trigger_signals: a new NOT NULL column or DB constraint on a table staging and prod share
a migration with raw SQL on another app's table, or role/privilege DDL
a feature flips an enablement flow for rows created under the old flow
staging and prod share one DB and the change alters the shape of rows (nesting, new parent links) that the deployed prod code also reads or writes
preventive_checks: Set db_default (or nullable + backfill) for new required fields; run sqlmigrate and reject bare ADD COLUMN NOT NULL on shared tables
Confirm every currently deployed code path honors a new constraint before it reaches the shared DB
Check rolsuper/CREATEROLE of the target DB role, and declare explicit cross-app migration dependencies
Ship a backfill with any behavior change and test it on pre-existing rows
Make the deployed code tolerate the new row shape first, or schedule the prod deploy right after staging; test the old code path against new-shape rows

FS-45.name: Agent turn ends waiting on an unverified async mechanism
FS-45.mechanism: A (sub)agent hands its completion to something asynchronous it never verified (its own Monitor watcher, a wakeup timer, a blocking debug call, a resumed run) and ends idle, wedged or silent with uncommitted edits. The orchestrator then waits or assumes failure instead of checking git and test state directly. Release automation adds background pollers that shell out to helpers in /tmp which vanish between sessions and then fail silently every cycle, background uploads and scratch dirs from a previous session with no completion record, a background subagent that crashed at launch, and a laptop that sleeps mid-pipeline. Fan-out lifecycle gaps compound it: more agents than the runtime's concurrency cap, stopped parents whose nested helpers keep running, and consumers launched when the producer's file appears rather than when it finishes.
trigger_signals: a worker's last action is starting a background run/Monitor and waiting for its notification
a blocking call against a live server or browser that can hang
a subagent silent for an unusually long time, or a promise of periodic updates on a timer
a subagent backgrounds its own long command and yields; multi-hour fan-out state held only in process; a fix loop planned around resuming agents via SendMessage
a background poll/loop shells out to a helper under /tmp or a scratch dir; resuming after hours or a session boundary on a background task's result; a long unattended release run on a laptop
dispatching three or more long-running worktree agents at once
an implementer has run many consecutive fix rounds in one session without committing (provider session/rate limits end it mid-round)
background implementer agents running when the parent session may hit a usage limit; planning to resume a subagent via SendMessage
dispatching more than ~20 background agents in one go (the runtime's concurrent-subagent cap)
stopping a parent agent whose brief lets it dispatch nested helpers
a producer agent still running while its output file already exists on disk, or several producers writing into one inbox that a later step globs
a bench, Playwright batch or suite whose last wall exceeded ~5 min run in the foreground: the Bash tool's 600 s limit silently moves it to the background
a next step planned as 'sleep N then read the log' (the harness blocks foreground sleep polling)
preventive_checks: Instruct workers to run verification synchronously or poll results themselves, never ending a turn on their own watcher
Background potentially hanging calls and poll with a timeout
When a subagent stalls, check git status/log and test results directly before relaunching
Put 'never background a command, run to completion' in every agent prompt template, checkpoint fan-out progress to a durable file, and confirm the resume tool is available before planning around it

Keep automation helpers in the repo's scripts/, make poll loops exit non-zero when a helper is missing, check a dispatched agent's output file size/mtime shortly after launch, treat a missing completion record as unknown and re-verify against the target system (ASC/Play), and run caffeinate for long unattended runs
Arm a per-worktree file-write staleness watch and check the session/rate budget before the fan-out
Commit after each discrete fix and write self-contained round briefs so a fresh agent can resume a round if the previous one dies
After any session restart check each in-flight worktree's git status before assuming work landed; hand off through a persisted report file a fresh agent reads, since SendMessage may be disabled
Check the runtime's concurrent-subagent cap and dispatch in batches under it
When cancelling a parent, list and stop its descendants too, then confirm nothing is still running
Dispatch consumers only on the producer's completion notification, never on file existence; aggregation reads a closed per-producer manifest instead of globbing a shared inbox
Size each foreground run under ~8 min, or launch with run_in_background plus a Monitor until-loop on the summary line; never end the turn before the summary and exit code exist
Integrators reject any lane report whose benchmark or suite result lacks the exit code and numbers

FS-46.name: Stage branch merged into a feature branch or promotion hop bypassed
FS-46.mechanism: In a multi-stage promotion chain (feature -> test -> dev -> staging -> main, with main backflowed down), a conflict or 'catch up' is resolved by merging a shared stage branch into the feature branch, cutting the branch from a stage, clicking GitHub 'Update branch', or pushing straight to a stage or main. The feature then carries the stage's unmerged backlog, so every later promotion PR drags dozens to hundreds of unrelated commits and conflicts. Separately, an unmerged or silently failed backflow breaks the 'target contains main' invariant, so PRs show phantom conflicts and pollution that get 'fixed' on the wrong branch.
trigger_signals: a promotion PR reports a conflict, or its diff/commit count is far larger than the commits you authored
about to run git merge origin/test|dev|staging (or GitHub 'Update branch') on a feature branch, or to branch from anything but origin/main
one feature branch feeds several promotion targets that have diverged from each other
about to push directly to a shared stage branch or main instead of opening the promotion PR, or to close a hop's PR and rely on backflow
a backflow PR (main -> dev/test/staging) is open, failed, or blocked by branch protection
preventive_checks: Before opening or fixing a promotion PR: git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main <target> (target contains main) and merge-base(<target>, <feature>) == origin/main tip; if not, merge or escalate the backflow gap instead of touching the feature branch

Never merge a stage branch into a feature branch; resolve conflicts by rebasing or cherry-picking only your own commits onto the target tip, then compare authored-commit count with git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD and read git diff --stat main...branch
Cut every feature/fix branch from fresh origin/main; when a branch feeds several targets, rebase onto their common ancestor and check a clean merge-tree against each target
Use the promotion PR for every hop (no direct pushes, no skipped hops); after a backflow or force-push, close/reopen open PRs so GitHub recomputes their base
Add a CI check that fails any feature branch whose history contains a merge commit from a stage branch

FS-47.name: Double-entry leg posted without its offsetting leg
FS-47.mechanism: The two legs of one accounting entry are produced by different functions, branches, events or entity save() hooks, each with its own guard: a date cutoff, a payee_type/source_type branch with a fallback on one side only, an early return meant for an unrelated sub-feature, an accrual leg deferred to a later payment event, a counter-leg that only another entity's save() creates, or a leg dated by a different rule than its counterpart. Any input that satisfies one side's condition but not the other's lands a lone leg and imbalances the balance sheet, which surfaces only in reconciliation weeks later.
trigger_signals: a ledger-posting function from a per-source-type family branches on payee type, source type, payment method or check type
one leg of a pair is created by a different entity's save() (Check, CreditPayment) or by a later event (payment of a credit expense)
a guard (early return, date cutoff, print/status gate, amount < epsilon skip) wraps only one of the legs, or sits above an independent sibling computation
a payment/clearing entity can have zero line items, or a bank categorization has no recognized transfer link
a new offsetting/suspense leg must net against an existing leg on the same day, or a bidirectional match writes only the counterpart
preventive_checks: Write a balance-invariant test per branch value (each payee_type, source_type, payment linkage, the degenerate empty entity): after posting, debits == credits and both legs share accounting_date and location
Post both legs from one function under the same guard and the same fallback strategy (both default, or both raise on an unrecognized enum value)
For accrual-type entities post the payable leg at accrual time and assert a credit expense with no payment yet still balances
Reject or route to a suspense/clearing account any input with no defined counter-leg (zero-item payment, bank-to-bank without a transfer link) instead of letting it fall through

Run a periodic audit query for source rows whose expected counterpart (a check record, a ledger entry, a POS purchase entry, a banking ledger entry) is missing, and assert both sides of a bidirectional match end symmetric

FS-48.name: Money sign, credit polarity and precision decided ad hoc in several layers
FS-48.mechanism: Direction of money is encoded more than one way (signed amount, abs(amount) plus a credit flag, per-path sign constants) and normalized in several layers: Transaction.save() force-sets credit for source types missing from a hand-maintained allowlist and auto-flips negative amounts, report code applies abs() after Sum(), filters use value < epsilon, dedupe keys use unsigned amounts, balance-sheet buckets recognize only listed account_types, and amounts live in FloatField or float accumulators mixed with Decimal. The positive, one-direction happy path balances; refunds, negative corrections, the other direction or a new source/account type post on the wrong side or vanish.
trigger_signals: a service sets an explicit credit flag, or passes a possibly negative amount, for a new or changed source_type
a new source_type or account_type constant is introduced (save() credit/sign allowlists, BS/P&L bucket constants)
abs(), '< 0.01'-style epsilon filters, or an unsigned amount in an aggregate, dedupe key or skip guard
a two-direction entity (disburse/receive, debit/credit) gets a validation or aggregate on one side only
FloatField money columns, float accumulators in scripts, output_field=DecimalField on a Sum/Window
a reviewer finds a polarity defect and downgrades it because it matches legacy behavior
preventive_checks: Test positive, negative and zero amounts for every source_type and both directions, asserting the persisted row's signed amount and credit flag after save(), not the value passed in

When adding a source type or account type, grep every allowlist and bucket constant (a transaction model's save() credit/sign lists, the asset/liability/other-expense type buckets) and add it; prefer inverting defaults so explicit flags win
Apply sign handling per row before aggregation, never abs() after Sum(); write an additivity test (full range == sum of sub-ranges) with mixed-sign rows
Use abs(x) < eps for near-zero checks, keep sign/direction in idempotency keys, and mirror every one-direction validation with the opposite-direction test
Store and sum money as Decimal (Cast inside the Sum/Window), start accumulators at Decimal('0'), and treat a legacy-matching polarity defect as blocking

FS-49.name: Delete-then-recreate resubmit strands previously posted rows
FS-49.mechanism: A resubmit/replace endpoint or rebuild implements 'update' as delete the parent and recreate children from the payload, as QuerySet.set() on an M2M, or as a skip when a value becomes zero. Children linked only by M2M survive as orphans with their posted transaction/ledger-entry legs, prior-version legs stay alive next to the new ones, a classification change leaves the other posting path's legs as zombies, validation runs after the delete, and day rebuilds delete every source type but recreate only some. Single-submit tests pass; the second resubmit, an edit to zero or a moved amount doubles or strands ledger rows.
trigger_signals: a submit/replace endpoint calls .filter(...).delete() on the parent before recreating children or before serializer validation
children linked to the parent by M2M rather than an owning FK with cascade; QuerySet.set() on a resync/relink path
a skip guard (if amt < 0.005: return/continue) inside an upsert-on-key writer
a mutable classification field (payee.is_employee, check trans_type, payment_type) decides which posting path owns a leg
a day-level delete-then-rebuild that deletes by date for all source types
a new report aggregates a child table that resubmits are known to orphan
preventive_checks: Update children in place by natural key (upsert-no-delete) and delete only rows absent from the payload, together with their posted legs, inside one transaction

Test resubmitting the same entry 2-3 times (including moving an amount between sibling child rows and editing a value to zero) and assert day_delta == 0 and no Expense/Deposit with an empty M2M still holds a live Transaction
Validate the whole payload before any delete; test that an invalid resubmit leaves the existing record intact
On a classification change, re-run every posting function gated by that field and clean up the legs of the path that no longer applies

Before a delete-then-rebuild, enumerate the source types present on the date and exclude any the rebuild cannot recreate (such as an opening-balance transaction); make each atomic unit one (location, day)
Aggregate child tables through the live parent link, never the raw child table

FS-50.name: Live-data fix applied without re-detecting and confirming the exact target rows
FS-50.mechanism: Ad hoc cleanup and heal scripts run against production pick their rows with a heuristic (a notes pattern, one negative condition such as 'no CreditPayment linked', all locations and all history, an id read out of an error tuple), from a detection snapshot taken before concurrent resubmits or background jobs changed the data, against a DB target inferred from env vars, with a dry run that doesn't gate every side effect, and without capturing evidence first. Legitimate compensating rows get deleted, material amounts are auto-applied like trivial ones, and forensic questions can no longer be answered.
trigger_signals: a script or --apply flag that deletes, strips or rewrites ledger/financial rows on a live DB
the row filter is a text pattern, a missing-relation condition, or 'same shape as location X'
the detection scan ran minutes or hours before the fix step, on a system users and jobs are writing to
one combined apply spans many locations/entities, or the dry run wraps DB writes in atomic() while an external call (S3) runs regardless
a 'who/when' forensic question is open about rows the fix will touch
an irreversible cascade delete previewed from Django's Collector.data
preventive_checks: Print and confirm an identifying fact from the connected DB (row counts, a known location name) before any --apply
Re-run the detector at the start of the fix step, check for concurrently running recon/backfill jobs, and re-query each target's live state (not just its id list)
Scope the fix to the rows confirmed broken; spot-check known-good locations against the candidate filter and check each row's precondition (is the leg truly one-sided?) before bulk stripping
Snapshot audit fields and the per-source diagnosis before any destructive step; print each target's business fields (amount, created_at, creator) before a hard delete

Run per entity/location instead of one opaque batch, route deletions above a materiality threshold to explicit approval, and gate every non-transactional side effect on the same --commit flag as the DB writes
Cross-check the preview against per-table row counts before and after the delete inside a rolled-back transaction; fast-deleted relations never appear in Collector.data

FS-51.name: Code handles one of several representations of the same fact
FS-51.mechanism: The same real-world fact is stored or transmitted several ways: a bank match as an FK or a batch M2M, account_type as a slug or a title-cased label, names with case/slug variants, location scope as a query param or a header, a file on the parent M2M or on per-section child fields, an orphan as a null FK or a detached non-null FK, URL scope under several param names. A query, merge key, guard, finder or test is written against the one representation the author saw first and declared exhaustive, so rows in the other representation slip through.
trigger_signals: a guard, finder or 'is matched/reconciled' check follows one relation path between two models
a grouping/merge key uses a raw type or name field that other code canonicalizes
request scope can arrive via query param or header; a guard allow-lists known URL param names
a cleanup is verified by searching for the exact string or anomaly signature named in the ticket
a cross-cutting feature (file tracking, audit) wired to the first model found carrying the field
a stored-file URL field can hold several URI schemes (s3://, gs://, https) and presigning is wired for only one; the field is rendered as an href in more than one component
an exclude/ignore list names one build-output dir (.next) in a repo that also holds suffixed variants (.next-live, .next-e2e, .next-verify)
comparing file paths that come from different producers (absolute vs repo-relative, ./ prefixes)
preventive_checks: Grep the schema for every FK/M2M/through relation linking the two models and every model carrying the field type; cover and test each path
SELECT DISTINCT the stored values of every key component org-wide before writing a merge key, and reuse the canonicalization the bucket router already uses
Resolve scope through the existing helper that honors every input channel (scope_to_locations / effective_location_ids) and test the header-only entry point
Verify cleanups with a broader case-insensitive/pattern search and check the sibling signature (null FK vs detached FK) before declaring done
Enumerate every link builder that targets a guarded route and test each param variant
Contract-test that every URL field in API responses starts with https:// for each configured storage backend, and grep every component that renders the field
Exclude by glob (.next*), then du -sh the staged context and compare it with the source size before shipping
Normalize both sides to resolved repo-relative paths before comparing, and test absolute, ./-prefixed and relative inputs

FS-52.name: Named-account get_or_create keyed on account_type forks duplicates as type strings drift
FS-52.mechanism: Chart-of-account rows are resolved or auto-created by get_or_create/update_or_create on (name, organization, location, account_type[, is_department]). When code changes the account_type a posting constant selects, a sibling caller omits account_type, legacy rows carry another spelling, or a merge leaves the keeper with a different type, the lookup misses and forks a live duplicate (or fails NOT NULL on create). Imports without dedupe and create/restore/replication paths recreate merged-away accounts, and retyping an account silently reclassifies every historical leg.
trigger_signals: get_or_create/update_or_create on a chart-of-accounts model whose lookup kwargs include account_type or other classification flags
changing the account_type string a posting constant, service or verify command uses
sibling posting functions calling the same account lookup helper with different parameters
merging or retyping accounts, or a bulk update into a column that is part of a unique constraint
a create/restore or corp-replication path that matches by (name, type)
preventive_checks: Put only identity fields (organization, location, name) in the lookup and classification in defaults=; test with a pre-existing same-name row of another type and assert no second live account
Pair every account_type constant change with a data migration that retypes existing same-name rows across every location tier, and patch recurring jobs' lookup keys together with any merge
Dry-run a collision query before bulk updates into unique-constrained fields and route twins to a merge path
Block or warn on account_type changes for accounts with posted legs (use a dated reclass entry); before merging across types, confirm both map to the same report bucket and polarity
Route create/restore/replication through one merge-aware helper that checks the account merge log

FS-53.name: Known fix or learned rule not made durable, so the same trap recurs
FS-53.mechanism: A root cause is found and fixed on a branch, filed as a chip, or taught by the user, but never carried to where it stops recurring: the fix sits unpromoted at some hop of the promotion chain (or pushed with no PR), the filed durable fix is never implemented, a pending migration is never landed, a faster tool or new safety rule never reaches the skill's default recipe or the scripts already written. The symptom keeps firing in production and is hand-healed, costing a round each time.
trigger_signals: the same symptom class shows up a second time, or a manual cleanup/sweep is being run again
a fix was 'pushed' but no promotion PR is open, or it has not reached main
a chip/TODO for the durable fix already exists for the error you are re-patching
the user states a rule correcting a mistake, or a new tool supersedes the documented recipe
every branch has to detect-and-ignore the same drift (unmade migration, scanner false positive)
a release helper or upload fix being recreated ad hoc for the second time; a session ending with a diagnosed fix deliberately held back
the same failure is flagged 'pre-existing, not my change' in two or more sessions
a process gap hit once in a parallel batch while other tickets in the same batch are still queued
preventive_checks: On the second occurrence treat the root-cause fix as blocking: report its branch -> PR -> promotion stage and count only 'merged to main and deployed' as done
Keep one visible list mapping recurring bug classes to fix branches and their promotion stage, and surface it every time the class fires
Write a user-taught rule or a new default tool into the skill/runbook immediately, then grep previously written fix scripts for violations
Land shared drift fixes (pending migration, scanner excludes, allowlists) once on main instead of working around them per branch
Commit hardened helpers into scripts/ on the first fix; write a held-back diagnosis and its next action to a ticket or memory before the session ends
Once a failure is confirmed pre-existing twice, fix it or file and link a ticket instead of re-flagging it
Add the learned step to every remaining brief and reviewer checklist in the batch immediately

FS-54.name: Stored copy of a financial figure not re-derived when its source changes
FS-54.mechanism: Figures are persisted as copies of their sources: a header total (total_deposit, credit_card_total, purchase cost) beside its line items, a daily entry's stored total_in/total_out shown on the calendar, a leg's accounting_date copied from a CreditPayment, posted ledger rows the balance sheet reads instead of recomputing, M2M mirrors keyed on the old (org, location, date). Only some write paths re-derive the copy (an entity's own save() re-posts only its own legs), so edits, re-keys and merges leave copies stale; consumers reading the copy and consumers recomputing live disagree, and 'balanced after rebuild' decays.
trigger_signals: a denormalized header/total field coexists with the child rows it summarizes, and different consumers read different ones
a leg's date/account/amount is copied from a related object at creation time
an edit to an entity drives legs that another process posted (no FK back to the entity)
an update can change the key (org, location, date) a derived mirror or M2M link is keyed on
a fix lives in save() and existing rows are expected to self-heal on the next rebuild; a merge edits posted legs but not the source pointer
preventive_checks: Derive totals from live child rows everywhere, or assert header == sum(lines) on save and run a periodic divergence query
For every stored copy list each writer of its inputs and each leg it drives; re-derive on every path or recompute on read; test edit-source-then-read-ledger
On key changes capture the old key before save and re-link/unlink both the old and the new key
Fix the upstream source pointer (the FKs that regenerate legs), not only posted legs, and ship an explicit backfill when a save()-time fix must apply to existing rows
Treat 'balanced' as a snapshot: schedule full-rebuild diffs for locations with ongoing edits

FS-55.name: Rule keyed on a proxy signal instead of the defining type, status or link
FS-55.mechanism: A posting rule, detector, cleanup or guard decides membership from something that usually correlates with the real condition: notes text ('TR FR/TO ...'), the existence of a downstream leg instead of the counterpart FK, an is_matched flag that ORs manual reconciliation with structural pairing, a denormalized date copy instead of the linked rows, a structural flag instead of account_type, every row in a source list without checking department_type, every status instead of the ones the balance sheet reads. Inputs where proxy and truth diverge are silently mis-posted, mis-flagged or deleted.
trigger_signals: a filter matches free text, notes or naming conventions to identify a class of financial row
a 'matched/unmatched' or 'safe to delete' decision inferred from a side effect or a conflated boolean
a business rule says 'only bank-type accounts' / 'only merchandise rows' / 'only REVIEWED' and the function never references that field
a lock or invariant check reads a denormalized copy on the mutated model
a build/config guard greps a whole file for a placeholder string instead of reading the one key it validates; a test-data cleanup selects rows by guessing their generated naming pattern
a cache-hit or fast-path early return tests only the fields one writer fills (transcript present) while the response promises more fields (summary, scores) that another path derives
classifying tests or endpoints as read-only by HTTP verb or URL while GET handlers may lazily get_or_create shared rows
preventive_checks: Filter on the defining field (account_type, department_type, status, the counterpart FK resolved in both directions) and add a fixture with the same text/shape but a different type/status that must be excluded
Split conflated booleans into separately named signals and have each consumer query the one it means
Enumerate every status/lifecycle value of the source model and state which ones the rule covers
Key cleanups and lookups on the canonical identity the sync writer uses ((source_type, source_id)) and resolve the real linked rows, not copies
Read the exact key path (plutil/jq) in config guards and test with a filled value plus a stale comment; mark test rows at creation and clean up by exact match, not by regex
Make the early-return condition list every field the response promises, and test with only the webhook-written fields populated
Back static read-only claims with a row-level DB write audit and flag get_or_create in GET handlers

FS-56.name: Ledger-wide change verified only where it was aimed
FS-56.mechanism: A posting-rule, polarity, exclusion or account_type change, or a rebuild/cleanup run, is checked only on the day, location or report that motivated it. The same computation feeds other days, periods, the balance-sheet footing and closed fiscal years; cleanup flags without date scoping, single-day rebuilds of multi-day entities, and recipes reused on a structurally different entity regress previously balanced data outside the target, which is found later as a 'new' imbalance.
trigger_signals: changing an account/polarity mapping, an exclusion from net income, or an account_type on existing data
running a rebuild/resync/--clean-dangling over a subset of days, or reusing a script validated on another entity
a rebuild range that includes closed periods or unverified/junk entities
the flagged day involves a cross-location bank transfer or another entity a generic rebuild doesn't handle
preventive_checks: Snapshot per-day balances (day_delta walk) and period-end totals for the whole affected range plus adjacent and closed periods, apply, then diff against the snapshot before calling it done
Measure balance-sheet footing on a couple of real locations with data in the category before changing a shared aggregate
Read the tool's documented scope and each flag's implementation (is it date-scoped?) before running; rebuild contiguously from a known-balanced opening date
Gate posting of unverified/junk entries and closed periods behind explicit checks; re-check day_delta immediately after each rebuild

FS-57.name: Reconciliation tooling re-implements production posting logic and drifts
FS-57.mechanism: Verify, resync, drift-detection and fast-check commands carry their own copy of which entities post which legs: a filter narrower than save()'s dispatch conditions, a step list missing helper calls the real view makes, a sync wired to one of two models behind a UI bucket, a mirror query without the reference's organization filter, counterpart lookups limited to the audited subset, exclusions encoding a rule a later feature changed, a rebuild that posts directly instead of calling save(). The tool's output then disagrees with production and is misread as a production bug or as a clean bill of health.
trigger_signals: writing or extending a verify/resync/detector command, or a 'fast' helper meant to mirror an authoritative computation
the tool calls service posting functions directly instead of the entity's save()/view flow
a feature changes what a source_type posts while detectors special-case that type
a detector resolves relationships from within its own filtered queryset
preventive_checks: Diff the tool's step and filter list against every ledger-posting call reachable from the entity's save()/view flow; reuse save() or the same service entry point instead of a partial copy
Assert equality with the reference computation over a swept historical range (including foreign-org and duplicate-leg data), not a hand-picked sample
Resolve counterparts against the full table, not the audited subset
When shipping a posting change, grep every reconciliation predicate that special-cases the source_type and add a regression test

FS-58.name: One financial total computed by independent code paths that disagree
FS-58.mechanism: The same number is computed separately for different consumers: balance sheet vs P&L (only one applies the cross-location suspense adjustment), statement subtotals vs grand total (abs per leaf vs signed sum), the over/short plug vs the ledger writer (different filters for negative rows or disabled entity types), a 'Cash Purchase' from two different models, a reconcile gate vs the apply step's persisted cost. Each path is internally consistent and tested alone; any input the paths treat differently makes the books or screens disagree.
trigger_signals: a report, plug or summary computes a figure that another report, poster or screen also computes
adding an adjustment, exclusion or new entity type to one computation of a shared total
a new cash-movement entity wired into the ledger but not into daily-entry derived totals (over/short, register)
a delta reported from two totals of the same metric
preventive_checks: Factor the figure into one shared function consumed by every path; derive grand totals from the displayed subtotal lines
Write a reconciliation test on fixtures containing negative corrections and every contributing entity: sum(posted legs) == stored daily-entry total, subtotals sum to net income, BS and P&L agree
When adding an entity or adjustment, list every derived total and decide explicitly whether each must include it
Label every reported total with its source query and assert both bases match before publishing a delta

FS-59.name: Model save() side effects unknown to the caller
FS-59.mechanism: Domain models override save() to auto-create or recompute related rows (Check.save() creates an Expense when expense is None and recomputes a linked purchase entry, Transaction.save() syncs the ledger entry, hooks re-query relations through custom managers). Callers that haven't read save() double-create rows in fixtures, spawn duplicates when linking FKs via save(), treat re-save as an idempotent restore, trigger the same recompute three times, assume an invariant the hook breaks, compare against an in-memory instance the update already mutated, or pass _id so the hook's re-query misses an uncommitted parent.
trigger_signals: calling .save() on a model with an overridden save() or signals from a script, fixture, rebuild or relink step
designing a match/link rule that assumes a related object is usually absent
a save()-time guard that inspects a field the same update may change
creating parent and child in one atomic block and assigning the FK by _id
adding a hook that calls a function other hooks already call
preventive_checks: Read the model's save()/signal chain before writing fixtures, rules, scripts or hooks that touch it, and assert related-table row counts before/after a dry run
Link FKs with queryset.update() when save() side effects are unwanted; assign the related object, not _id, when save() re-reads the relation
Capture previous values from the DB (not the mutated instance) for save()-time cleanup guards
Don't use re-save as a restore unless save() replays stored values; add a call-count test for recomputes per save

FS-60.name: Read after write or guard read routed to a lagging replica
FS-60.mechanism: Production routes ORM reads to a read replica (ReplicaRouter/PinningReplicaRouter, USE_REPLICA=1) while tests and dev run one database. A read of a row just written in the same request or script, a lazy FK re-query, a soft-delete cascade walker, a bulk sync re-reading its output, or a guard feeding a permission/delete/merge decision hits the replica before replication, so it sees stale or missing rows, raises false integrity errors or makes a stale decision. Fixes pin the quoted line but not the other reads feeding the same decision.
trigger_signals: a handler, script or bulk sync writes and then reads the same or related rows
a read feeds a permission check, lock, delete/merge guard, or the verification of a write
the file already uses .using('default') on neighbouring reads
third-party code (soft-delete cascade, related managers) reads without the router hint
preventive_checks: Pin every read that follows a write or gates an irreversible decision to primary (.using('default'), select_related on the write connection), tracing the full data flow into the guard
Run delete/merge/permission tests with USE_REPLICA=1 or a replica-simulating router, and assert the active router class in ops scripts before trusting a verification read
When fixing one replica-lag finding, grep for the same write-then-read pattern org-wide instead of patching one call site

FS-61.name: Startup path echoes production credentials into captured output
FS-61.mechanism: Settings/startup code prints credentials fetched from the secret manager, and a shared ops box's login-shell profile echoes the prod DB credential as a banner. Any SSM, CI or agent command run through manage.py shell or a login shell (bash -lc, sudo -i, ssh with a profile) captures the secret into logs and transcripts. The trap is known and noted in memory but not fixed, so it recurs on every remote-ops task.
trigger_signals: about to run a command on a remote box via a login shell, sudo -i, or manage.py shell
settings/startup code logs or prints resolved secrets
memory notes a credential-echo trap on a box you are about to use
preventive_checks: Invoke remote commands with a non-login shell (bash --noprofile --norc, no -l/-i) and prefer management commands or script files over manage.py shell
Grep settings/startup code and the box's shell profile for print/log/echo of secret values and remove them at the source; rotate any credential that appeared in output
Track the leak as a blocking ops item, not a memory note, and scrub secret-shaped strings from output before surfacing it

FS-62.name: Bug class fixed in one template-copied sibling survives in the others
FS-62.mechanism: A family of near-identical functions for different entity types (one ledger-posting function per source type such as deposit, expense, merchandise and fuel; a P&L report module beside a balance-sheet report module; backfill scripts beside the pipeline) was built by copying one template. A bug in the template (child-row date/location/organization instead of the parent daily entry's, update_or_create keyed on one FK, a NULL-excluding filter, abs() after aggregate, a status gate for one subtype) is fixed where it was reported, and the other copies keep it until each is rediscovered in a later reconciliation round.
trigger_signals: fixing a bug in one function whose name follows a family pattern (a shared posting-function prefix, *_view, fix_*)
the fix changes how a field is sourced (date, location, organization) or how a lookup is keyed
a gate or rule exists for one subtype (expense checks) of a model with sibling subtypes
preventive_checks: After the fix, grep every sibling in the family (and adjacent backfill/fix scripts) for the same pattern and fix or document each before calling it done
Diff sibling functions line by line for field sourcing and lookup keys, and enumerate every field copied from the wrong source, not just the one that triggered the bug
Add one regression test per sibling or subtype, and extract the shared piece into a helper

FS-63.name: Entity identity matched on a non-identifying attribute
FS-63.mechanism: Scripts, importers and pickers decide which real-world entity a row refers to by a display name, .first() of several candidates, or a (payee, amount, date) coincidence, while the data has names repeated across orgs/locations, several bank accounts per location, dangling duplicates from delete-then-recreate, and legitimate same-amount instruments. The opposite error also occurs: exact FK equality treats punctuation-variant duplicate payees as different entities. The wrong row gets linked, voided, skipped or created.
trigger_signals: resolving a location, account or bank account by name or .first() in a multi-org / multi-account setting
treating rows as duplicates because payee/amount/date match
a match predicate in a reconciliation script that lacks the identity field (employee name, check number)
guarding on FK equality in a domain with known near-duplicate master records
a data migration dedups or groups by a business key without the tenant/repository id
a reconcile/reindex step that runs per page or partition while row identity is unique per document; match keys that are mutable attributes or list positions
output files or ids keyed on a value that repeats across sources (session id in two dirs) or derived from enumeration order while another artifact persists references to them
preventive_checks: Resolve by a unique key (id, check/invoice number) scoped by organization and location; when the input lacks one, require the column or flag every ambiguous row instead of taking .first()
Query all candidates sharing the name across orgs and confirm against a reference point the user gave before creating or mutating
Spot-check a known-unique row to confirm the match predicate discriminates; filter to currently linked rows (e.g. daily_entries__isnull=False) in models with dangling duplicates
Ask before treating a same-amount/same-date record as a duplicate
Include the tenant key in dedup group-bys and test the same canonical id present in two tenants in different states
Match on the stable id at the identity's full uniqueness scope (document, not page); test moving content across partitions, editing matched attributes, and inserting/renumbering items
Persist ids once into the source records and key outputs on (source, id)

FS-64.name: Destructive or prod-wide write started without an explicit go-ahead for that scope
FS-64.mechanism: An agent treats a feasibility question, a clean dry run, one subagent's widened success, or a broad earlier approval as permission for a production write at a larger scope; read-only subagents run the --apply recipe from muscle memory; sibling fan-out agents keep applying while a policy question raised by one of them is pending. The write lands before the user has confirmed its scope.
trigger_signals: the user asked 'can you' / 'is it feasible' rather than 'do it'
a dry run just succeeded and the next command is --apply across many locations/days
a subagent reports out-of-scope findings or hits a policy gate during a fan-out
dispatching identify-only agents whose normal recipe includes a write flag
spawning write-capable parallel workers from a broad queue
preventive_checks: Name the exact scope (count of locations/days/rows) and wait for an explicit go-ahead before any --apply beyond the agreed batch
Ban the write flag in read-only agent prompts and require the agent to echo each command before running it against prod
When one agent hits a policy-defining gate, pause every sibling until it is resolved; confirm widened scope with the user before applying it to the rest of the batch
Make write queues stoppable per item

FS-65.name: Which host, checkout or branch serves an environment assumed
FS-65.mechanism: Boxes keep a manual git checkout beside the CodeDeploy-served directory, services track a branch other than the one just pushed, a staging hostname hits the dev backend while sharing the prod DB, and only one box ships logs to the central store.
