Verification, restarts, migration checks and forensics run against whichever host or directory is at hand and produce clean-looking but wrong answers ('deployed', 'no logs', 'migrated').
trigger_signals: verifying deployed code or migration state on a box, or advising 'restart to pick up the change'
searching a central log store for a non-prod hostname's traffic
installing a long-running service against an ad hoc checkout while the pipeline is blocked
about to conclude that evidence or logs are unrecoverable
a prod manage.py run after sourcing .env.prod without --settings or an exported DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE
preventive_checks: Read the service's systemd unit WorkingDirectory and venv, then check git -C <that dir> rev-parse HEAD and its branch before verifying or restarting
Confirm which backend host serves each hostname and whether its logs ship before searching; enumerate known hosts (deploy config, DNS, known_hosts) before declaring data unrecoverable
Track any service pointed at a manual checkout as temporary and re-point it at the deploy target before calling the rollout done
Pass --settings explicitly and print the resolved settings module and DB host as the first output line of any prod ops command

FS-66.name: Session-scoped cloud or CLI credentials assumed still valid
FS-66.mechanism: AWS SSO tokens and CLI OAuth logins expire within hours, and long sessions, sub-sessions and bench runs inherit the same expired state. Investigations, downloads and tunnels start without an identity check and fail mid-flight, sometimes after partial work, and the same expiry recurs after each multi-hour gap.
trigger_signals: starting remote diagnostics, an SSM/tunnel session, a cloud download or a local bench run
a multi-hour gap since the last cloud command in the session
spawning a sub-session that inherits local CLI auth
an admin task starts with gcloud compute ssh or other gcloud calls under an org policy that forces periodic interactive reauth
a gcloud scp/ssh production write late in a long session
a merged PR's deploy step queued hours after the gcloud login in the same agent session
preventive_checks: Run a cheap identity check first (aws sts get-caller-identity, CLI auth status) and ask the user to re-auth up front if it fails
Re-check at the start of every task that opens a new tunnel/SSM session, and short-circuit dependent runs on the first auth failure instead of retrying each blind
Keep a documented fallback path (SSH key) for remote access
Check gcloud auth validity first and surface reauth immediately; prefer a service-account identity for headless admin scripts
Run gcloud auth print-access-token before staging files and again right before the write
Run gcloud auth print-access-token right before any queued deploy step and use a deploy-scoped service account instead of a personal OAuth session for automated deploys

FS-67.name: On-device check runs a stale JS bundle or a dev-client path unlike the shipped build
FS-67.mechanism: On-device verification of an Expo/React Native fix runs code other than the edited source: Metro's transform cache or a quick rebuild serves the old transform, an Expo dev-client loads JS from its expo-updates store so an injected main.jsbundle is ignored (and a plain bundle injected into a Hermes release build crashes on launch), Fast Refresh patches a leaf but keeps parent closures holding old handlers, Metro restarted with CI=1 has Fast Refresh off, a warm dev-client drops Linking url events, and every full reload wipes in-memory auth. The old behavior reproduces and is read as 'the fix didn't work', or a pass is trusted on the wrong build. Mobile sibling of FS-02.
trigger_signals: on-device behavior after a fix matches the pre-fix behavior exactly, even after a rebuild
about to verify through a bundle-inject or 'fast rebuild' shortcut, or the installed app is an Expo dev-client rather than a release/embedded build
the fix changes a handler captured in a closure (onSubmitEditing chain, ref callback, router handler) above the file just edited
a subagent or script (re)starts Metro, possibly with CI=1 or other non-interactive flags
testing a deep link (magic link, universal link) against an app that is already foregrounded in a dev-client
several files will change during one on-device session in an app whose auth uses in-memory persistence (Firebase inMemoryPersistence)
two consecutive code edits produce pixel-identical screenshots, especially after a simulator/device relaunch
preventive_checks: Before trusting an on-device result, prove the running bundle contains the change: grep the built/served bundle for a marker string unique to the new code, or restart Metro with --reset-cache

Know the build type first: Debug dev-client -> iterate through Metro; release/embedded -> rebuild; never inject a plain JS bundle into a Hermes release build; clear .expo-internal / the updates store on dev-client builds
After focus-chain, closure or router logic changes, force a full app relaunch instead of trusting Fast Refresh
Forbid CI=1 when handing Metro to a subagent and confirm Fast Refresh with a trivial edit before trusting reload results
Cold-start the app (force-quit, then open the link) when testing deep links against a dev-client so getInitialURL() handles them
With in-memory auth, batch edits before a reload-triggering pass (or keep a persistent test session) instead of re-authenticating per edit
Show a build/commit freshness marker in the UI (or check Metro's request log for this device) as step 1 whenever two edits look identical

FS-68.name: User-facing copy, enum labels or digits bypass the localization layer
FS-68.mechanism: In a localized app (i18next t(), Arabic with Arabic-Indic digits) new or extended components render literal English strings, raw enum/data keys (Object.keys, WANT/FIT), SDK-provided strings (RevenueCat priceString) or Intl output directly, or compare a localized options list against an untranslated stored token. Whole components written before the i18n pass never call t(). English QA looks complete; the gap surfaces only when a user reaches that flow in Arabic, one screen at a time.
trigger_signals: a .tsx file that renders <Text> has zero t( calls, or a JSX text node / prop default is a quoted capitalized English string
a component renders enum values, object keys or status codes as display text
a new screen shows a number or price from a third-party SDK (RevenueCat, StoreKit) or formats digits with Intl.NumberFormat
a picker checks whether a stored raw value is a known option by looking it up in a list of translated labels
extending a component or screen that predates the app's i18n retrofit
a next-intl useTranslations(namespace) whose keys were authored under another component's JSON path
preventive_checks: Grep touched and sibling files for literal capitalized strings in JSX and for .tsx files with <Text> but no t( before calling an i18n change done; run the same check in CI or the pre-release checklist

Map every enum/key shown to users through t() with one key per value; compare canonical tokens, never localized labels (de-localize one side first), and unit-test that a stored canonical value does not produce a duplicate option
Route every displayed number and store price through the shared localizeDigits()/price component; on Hermes do not rely on Intl numberingSystem options or -u-nu- locale tags, which iOS Hermes ignores
QA every touched screen in Arabic on device, including sheets and every variant (each paywall gate reason), not only the screen that was reported
Assert rendered label text, not only testid presence, and lint for translation namespaces with zero matching keys

FS-69.name: Store purchase, offer or redemption flow built on assumed platform semantics
FS-69.mechanism: App Store / Google Play / RevenueCat flows are built or explained from memory: the generic play.google.com/redeem page is assumed to accept subscription offer codes, RevenueCat presentCodeRedemptionSheet() wraps a deprecated StoreKit-1 API that resolves without presenting anything, a purchase completed outside the app is never synced (no syncPurchases on foreground), a recreated ASC offer silently defaults to one territory, and sandbox/TestFlight redemptions never reach the production entitlement store. Console navigation is asserted to the user without seeing it. Promise resolution and unit tests pass; only a real account on a real device against the live store exposes it. Store-specific sibling of FS-42.
trigger_signals: implementing or changing a purchase, offer-code, promo or redeem path on iOS or Android
calling an SDK method that bridges a native store sheet (presentCodeRedemptionSheet and similar) and checking it only by promise resolution or a log line
the purchase or redemption now happens outside the app (deep link, browser, App Store / Play page)
recreating or editing a live App Store Connect subscription offer, price or territory set through the API
about to tell the user where an option lives in App Store Connect, Play Console or RevenueCat without seeing their screen
billing sync reports synced:false while users report successful redemptions
preventive_checks: Before building, read the store's current documentation for the exact product type (subscription vs one-time) and code type (custom vs one-time) and cite it; then test end to end with a real account on a real device
Verify the visible effect on device (sheet shown, entitlement flipped), not promise resolution; check the SDK changelog/issues for wrappers around deprecated OS APIs
Whenever entitlement can be granted outside the SDK purchase call, call Purchases.syncPurchases()/restore on the next foreground and test the external round trip
When recreating an ASC offer, diff the new territory list against the old one before deactivating the old offer and abort if it shrinks
Log the receipt environment (sandbox vs production) on every billing sync call and watch the ratio
Ask for a screenshot or WebFetch the platform's current docs before giving console navigation steps; flag region- or config-gated options as unverified

FS-70.name: Mobile behavior verified on one OS or only on the Simulator
FS-70.mechanism: A React Native change is checked on one platform (often the Android emulator or one iPhone simulator) and reported fixed for both, but iOS and Android diverge: iOS presents only one Modal at a time, Android's LinearGradient ignores border radius and overflow set on itself, contentInset exists only on iOS, a Maestro flow hardcodes one platform's appId. The Simulator also differs from devices: native store sheets don't render, 'Connect Hardware Keyboard' suppresses the soft keyboard, and automated text injection drops characters. The user on the other platform or on a real device finds it.
trigger_signals: a layout, modal/sheet, gradient, keyboard or native-SDK change about to be reported done with screenshots from one platform
a component opens a second Modal (image picker, sheet) while another Modal is visible
a shared Maestro/e2e flow file with a literal appId or a platform-specific selector
the user reports a control 'does nothing' that works on the developer's simulator
verification depends on the soft keyboard or on typing long strings into the iOS Simulator
keyboard-avoidance fixes look identically broken across rebuilds on the iOS Simulator
preventive_checks: Screenshot-verify every RN UI fix on both iOS and Android (and a real device for native sheets, gradients and keyboard) or state explicitly which platform was checked
Never stack RN Modals: close the first or render the second inside it, and test nested modal/sheet flows on iOS
Parameterize appId per platform in Maestro flows and smoke-run each new flow on both platforms before using it as a RED/GREEN gate
On a repeated 'not working' report, gather device logs, viewport width and platform capability before reasserting that it works
Before keyboard tests on the iOS Simulator turn off Connect Hardware Keyboard; for text-heavy input use a real device or chunked typing with read-back
Make 'Connect Hardware Keyboard off' step 0 of any keyboard bug checklist; if keyboardDidShow never fires, check the setting before changing code

FS-71.name: Store build inputs taken from local state instead of asserted against the release target
FS-71.mechanism: A TestFlight/App Store/Play build takes its marketing version, build number, branch and API environment from whatever the local tree holds: app.json's version (already approved, or its train closed after READY_FOR_SALE), a build number left from an earlier pre-fix build, the branch a shared working tree happens to be on, and a .env EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL still pointing at staging. The archive/upload fails late and costs a full re-archive, or it succeeds and ships the wrong code or backend under a version the user is told is live.
trigger_signals: starting a release pipeline from app.json's version/buildNumber without querying App Store Connect or Play first
app.json already carries an uncommitted build-number value before a release run, especially after an interrupted or resumed build
the previous marketing version is approved or READY_FOR_SALE and only the build number changed
a release build runs in a shared working tree or right after switching branches, with .env edited independently of the branch
the API URL lives in both eas.json env blocks and a .env/.env.local read by custom release scripts; a release script exports EXPO_PUBLIC_* vars one by one (grep/cut) instead of sourcing the env file
preventive_checks: Before archiving, query ASC appStoreVersions/builds (and Play tracks) for the highest approved/READY_FOR_SALE version and highest build, and bump the marketing version strictly above any closed train
Mint a fresh, monotonically unique build number per pipeline run (for example a timestamp) instead of trusting app.json
Begin every release script with an explicit checkout of the named release branch and print the HEAD SHA
Fail the build when EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL (or any other baked-in env) does not match the production host for a store-bound build
Before saying 'live', confirm the exact build number/commit attached to the live store version
Keep one source for baked-in env and run the placeholder guard on every build path (EAS profiles and local scripts)
Source the full env file in release scripts and assert after the build that the bundle contains every required EXPO_PUBLIC_* key

FS-72.name: Bottom clearance (safe area, tab bar, keyboard) applied zero times or twice
FS-72.mechanism: Bottom spacing in React Native comes from several layers that may already reserve it: React Navigation shortens scenes above a non-absolute tab bar, iOS ScrollView contentInset and paddingBottom both add space, useSafeAreaInsets must be added in every layout branch, and on Android edge-to-edge (Expo SDK 54 default) adjustResize is a no-op so KeyboardAvoidingView never lifts a pinned footer. Code adds its own padding without checking which layer already handles it, or drives margin from a raw keyboard-height listener with no clamp. It looks right on the device checked and leaves gaps, home-indicator overlaps or hidden Save buttons elsewhere.
trigger_signals: a style object branches (inline/modal/full-screen) and only one branch adds insets.bottom
a shared hook adds tab-bar height as padding, or a ScrollView sets both paddingBottom and contentInset.bottom
a pinned footer relies on KeyboardAvoidingView in an Android edge-to-edge app without react-native-keyboard-controller
layout margin driven directly by a Keyboard event height
a form screen with text inputs uses a vertically centred or flexGrow contentContainerStyle
preventive_checks: Before adding clearance, render with padding 0 to see what the navigator and safe area already reserve; pick one mechanism per screen and grep for co-occurring paddingBottom + contentInset.bottom
Add insets.bottom in every layout branch of a bottom-pinned control
On Android edge-to-edge use react-native-keyboard-controller (or explicit keyboard padding) and screenshot with the keyboard open on a real Android device
Clamp keyboard-derived heights to a fraction of the window height and reset them on keyboardDidHide and when AppState leaves 'active'
Top-align input forms (top-aligned ScrollView plus KeyboardAvoidingView); a centred layout has no overflow for any avoidance technique to reveal

FS-73.name: Native build started without a host preflight (SDK path, UTF-8 locale, disk, gitignored config)
FS-73.mechanism: Local iOS/Android builds depend on host state that a fresh shell, a fresh worktree or a cache wipe removes: ANDROID_HOME and android/local.properties sdk.dir (deleted by expo prebuild --clean), a UTF-8 LANG/LC_ALL for CocoaPods pod install, free disk after repeated archives fill DerivedData/Archives, and gitignored native config (google-services.json, GoogleService-Info.plist, .env) that exists only in the main tree. The build fails minutes in, often in the middle of a release pipeline.
trigger_signals: first Android/iOS build in a session or in a fresh worktree, or right after wiping DerivedData, ios/build or Expo caches
about to run expo prebuild --clean or pod install from a non-login or background shell
several archive/build cycles already ran in this session
the app depends on gitignored native config files
more than two or three full native rebuilds planned in one session on a laptop disk; an opaque Gradle daemon or build-tool error mid-session
preventive_checks: Run a preflight before every native build: ANDROID_HOME/adb set and android/local.properties has sdk.dir, LANG=en_US.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 exported, df -h shows headroom, and every required gitignored file exists
Make that preflight (including restoring local.properties after prebuild --clean) an explicit step of the release script, not a manual afterthought
Copy every gitignored config the build needs from the main tree into a fresh worktree before its first build
Clear stale DerivedData and old .xcarchive files between repeated archive attempts
Run df -h before each rebuild and clear regenerable caches (DerivedData, Gradle build outputs) between builds, not after a failure

FS-74.name: Fixed lineHeight near fontSize clips Arabic and display glyphs
FS-74.mechanism: Text styles pin a numeric lineHeight equal or close to fontSize (9/9, 15/18, 22/26), tuned for Latin text. Arabic fonts such as Cairo have taller ascenders and diacritics, and large display headings put the cap height at the line-box edge, so glyphs are cut. The symptom reads like layout overflow, so the first fixes change flexShrink/flexWrap, and the bug recurs component by component as users find each screen.
trigger_signals: a text style sets an explicit numeric lineHeight at or below about 1.2x fontSize on user-facing copy in an Arabic-capable app
a large display/heading style with lineHeight === fontSize
a user reports text 'clipped' in a pill, badge or name while its container looks correctly sized
preventive_checks: Route text styles through the shared rtlLineHeight() helper (or give at least 1.2x fontSize headroom) instead of literal lineHeight values
When one clipping bug is found, audit every literal lineHeight in the app once instead of fixing per report
Before changing layout for 'clipping', zoom into the glyphs in Arabic on device to tell vertical font clipping from overflow

FS-75.name: Generated native project or build cache not regenerated after a config, asset or cache change
FS-75.mechanism: In Expo projects ios/ and android/ are generated by expo prebuild (often gitignored), and New-Architecture codegen headers live in DerivedData/ios/build. Icon, splash, app.json and config-plugin changes need prebuild --clean on both platforms, incremental xcodebuild reuses an already compiled Assets.car, a DerivedData wipe needs prebuild/pod install before archiving, and helper scripts may not run prebuild at all. Skipping regeneration ships stale assets on one platform or fails the archive on missing ReactCodegen headers.
trigger_signals: icon, splash, app.json, config-plugin or native dependency changes followed by an incremental build
DerivedData or ios/build was deleted and the next step is an 'archive-only' shortcut
a rebrand/asset change verified only on the platform currently open in a simulator
a runbook says a release script runs prebuild, and nobody has read the script body this session
preventive_checks: After any asset/config/plugin change or cache wipe, run expo prebuild --clean for BOTH ios and android (then pod install) before building; never trust incremental xcodebuild for assets
Diff each platform's generated asset hash/mtime against the new source and cold-install to check the launch frames
Read a release helper's actual body before relying on a runbook's description of it, and correct the runbook

FS-76.name: Native capability added without its signing, entitlement, packaging or store-policy counterpart
FS-76.mechanism: A native permission, entitlement, system-store field or packaging option is added for a feature, but its counterpart outside the JS code is not updated: a provisioning profile pinned in exportOptions.plist predates new entitlements (Associated Domains, Sign in with Apple), Play requires a declaration for FOREGROUND_SERVICE_* permissions, writing CNContact.note needs a restricted Apple entitlement the Simulator doesn't enforce, and expo.useLegacyPackaging=false leaves no fallback when the arm64-v8a split is missing. Debug builds and simulators pass; export signing, store review, real devices or production crash reports catch it, often releases later.
trigger_signals: a config plugin or AndroidManifest change adds a permission on Play's declared-permission list (FOREGROUND_SERVICE*, background location, exact alarms)
adding an entitlement or capability while exportOptions.plist pins a named provisioning profile
a native module writes Contacts/Calendar/Photos fields and has been tested only on the Simulator
changing APK/AAB packaging (useLegacyPackaging, ABI splits, device targeting)
the app requests a sensitive permission (location) and the repo keeps its own privacy doc of intended App Privacy label values
preventive_checks: Use automatic (Xcode-managed) signing for release export so entitlement changes regenerate the profile
File the Play Console declaration in the same work item that adds a policy-gated permission, not at release time
Check Apple's restricted-entitlement list for every system-store field written and smoke-test the write on a real device
Inspect the built AAB/APK device targeting (bundletool) for every target ABI including arm64-v8a, and install on a real arm64 device with the configuration Play will serve
Before every submission diff the live App Store Connect App Privacy labels against the repo's privacy doc field by field and remove declared-but-unused data types

FS-77.name: Gated app flow (onboarding, paywall, restore) kept consistent only by navigation order
FS-77.mechanism: Onboarding, paywall and navigation-restore behavior is encoded as navigation rather than as state each screen checks: a route allowlist in a guard, 'we never navigate here when subscribed', one completion side effect repeated per exit path, a saved stack replayed with router.push. A new entry route missing from the allowlist bounces users back, a new exit path skips marking onboarding complete, a paywall renders for an already-Pro user reached through skip or the back stack, and a cold-start restore replays every saved frame while an unguarded state listener re-persists it.
trigger_signals: adding a screen or entry point reachable from inside a gated flow (onboarding, auth wall, paywall)
adding a new way to exit a wizard step alongside the existing purchase/continue paths
a paywall/pricing screen reachable by more than one path (wizard, deep link, back stack)
a nav-state restore effect issuing several router.push/replace calls while a state-change listener persists navigation
preventive_checks: Write a router-guard unit test asserting the new route is not redirected in each incomplete-flow state before wiring the UI entry point
Route every exit of a gated step through one shared completion function (for example completeOnboardingStep()) and test each exit
Make gated screens self-guard at render time on the real state (effective_plan, onboarding_completed_at) instead of relying on navigation
Cap restored navigation to [tab, leaf] and suppress persistence listeners while a restore replay runs; test the back-press count after a cold start

FS-78.name: Manual RTL flip stacked on a layer that already auto-mirrors
FS-78.mechanism: Under I18nManager RTL, Yoga mirrors left/right and absolute positions, React Navigation's native header back button and some icon sets mirror themselves, and custom icon components do not. Code adds scaleX(-1) or I18nManager.isRTL left/right swaps on top of an auto-mirroring layer, which double-flips back to the wrong direction; a fix that then removes the flip everywhere breaks the path that doesn't mirror. Each render path behaves differently and only an RTL device check shows it.
trigger_signals: a style checks I18nManager.isRTL to swap left/right, borderLeft/borderRight or margins
a directional icon (chevron, arrow, back) wrapped in scaleX(-1) or an rtlFlip helper
the same glyph rendered through a native navigation header and through a custom shared icon component
preventive_checks: Use logical start/end properties (marginStart, borderStartWidth, start) instead of manual isRTL swaps
Before adding a manual flip, check on device in RTL whether that exact render path already mirrors
When fixing one RTL direction bug, grep every render path of that icon and verify each one on device

FS-79.name: Sync or offline state decided from an empty, transient or proxy remote signal
FS-79.mechanism: An offline-first sync engine treats what the remote returned as the whole truth: a prune step deletes local rows absent from the pull response, so an empty or partial response (transient failure, scope change) wipes the device's data; a guard against a 'suspiciously empty' response counts records while the backend always injects a builtin/sentinel record; the offline banner trusts NetInfo.isConnected (false negatives on the iOS Simulator, stale on devices) instead of probing the backend. Happy-path sync tests pass; users lose local data or see a false offline state. Server-side, a lenient parser that maps invalid input to empty feeds a reindex that deletes every row.
trigger_signals: a pull/sync step computes stale = local minus remote and deletes from that set
a sanity guard uses list.length on a response that can contain builtin/system rows
offline UI branches on NetInfo.isConnected or isInternetReachable alone
a request gate (react-query onlineManager or similar) pauses every request on isInternetReachable
a server-side sync/reindex that deletes rows absent from parsed input, fed by a parser that returns empty on invalid input
preventive_checks: Write the empty-response and error-response tests first and assert zero local deletions; treat an empty list as unknown and prune only on explicit tombstones or a confirmed per-row 404
Exclude sentinel/builtin records before counting, and test the case where only the sentinel is present
Drive offline UI from a real /health probe of the app's own backend, using NetInfo only as a hint
Never use isInternetReachable as a hard request gate (it cannot succeed on the Simulator); gate on isConnected plus a real backend probe
Parse strictly (invalid input raises, never returns empty) and refuse a destructive sync on empty input unless it is explicitly confirmed

FS-80.name: Temporary debug bypass or backdoor left in a shipped auth path
FS-80.mechanism: A shortcut added for local testing, such as an impersonation hook that signs in with a token read from .env or a `false &&` short-circuit on the email-verification gate, is gated on a token's presence or on nothing at all instead of __DEV__ plus a default-off flag. It rides along into store builds and production and silently disables a security control until someone notices.
trigger_signals: an auth/verification condition gains a literal true &&/false && prefix, or a TEMP/DEV/BYPASS/HACK comment
the app entry (_layout.tsx) imports a debug module that reads a secret or token from EXPO_PUBLIC_* env
about to cut a store release after a debugging session that touched auth
preventive_checks: Gate any dev-only auth behavior on __DEV__ plus an explicit env flag that defaults off, never on a token's presence
Before every release grep the diff for true &&/false &&, TEMP/BYPASS markers and EXPO_PUBLIC_*TOKEN reads, and grep the release bundle for the debug module's marker
Keep a test asserting the security gate rejects the unverified/unauthorized case

FS-81.name: Next.js build output (.next) shared between dev and e2e, or served stale by next start
FS-81.mechanism: A Next.js app's dev server and the e2e or verify harness write the same default distDir (.next), and the Playwright webServer runs `next start` (often with reuseExistingServer) against whatever build is there. A concurrent `next build` deletes chunks from under the running dev server (MODULE_NOT_FOUND on vendor-chunks, ENOENT on app-build-manifest.json, 500s), `next start` keeps serving a baked build with no watcher so edits never appear, and status-only health checks keep returning 200. The failures look like bundler bugs or real regressions, so fixes are made against the wrong build.
trigger_signals: a Next.js app whose dev server and Playwright webServer (or a verify build) both default to .next, with no per-purpose distDir
the e2e webServer command is `next start` / start:e2e with no preceding `next build`, combined with reuseExistingServer
intermittent MODULE_NOT_FOUND on vendor-chunks, ENOENT on app-build-manifest.json or 'Could not find a production build' while another agent's suite runs
a monitor or health check that only curls routes for 200 on a shared dev port that another process can restart
an e2e failure shows old copy or CSS right after a source change
preventive_checks: Give dev, e2e and verify builds separate distDirs through an env var (for example NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-e2e) from the start
Make the e2e webServer command build before it starts, or set reuseExistingServer: false when validating a rendering change; on any stale-looking result kill the port and rebuild before re-running
Check the serving process's command line (next dev vs next start) and prove live reload by adding and then removing a throwaway route, not by a 200
Before blaming the bundler for MODULE_NOT_FOUND/ENOENT, check .next artifact mtimes and which process last wrote them

FS-82.name: Update endpoint assigns raw request data onto the model instead of going through the serializer
FS-82.mechanism: A PATCH/update view or service applies the client dict with setattr (or .update(**data)) while create goes through the DRF serializer. The update path skips type coercion, so wire-format strings reach numeric business-rule comparisons and 500; it skips Serializer.validate() and the ValidationError-to-400 mapping; and it has no writable-field allowlist, so clients can set server-managed fields such as status. Create-path tests pass, and nothing sends PATCH with wire-format strings or forbidden fields.
trigger_signals: an update/PATCH view or service function takes a raw dict and calls setattr in a loop, queryset.update(**data) or obj.__dict__.update
business-rule validation lives in Serializer.validate() but the update path never instantiates the serializer with partial=True
a model with server-managed fields (status, workflow state, computed totals, owner) is exposed through a PATCH endpoint
preventive_checks: Route create and update through the same serializer (partial=True for PATCH) with is_valid(raise_exception=True); grep views and services for setattr over request data
Write a PATCH test that sends wire-format strings for every numeric/rate field and asserts 400, never 500, on a rule violation
Write a mass-assignment test per PATCH endpoint that tries every server-managed/read-only field and asserts it is ignored or rejected; declare read_only_fields explicitly

FS-83.name: Shared CSS class, combinator or container rule reused beyond the shape it was written for
FS-83.mechanism: Plain CSS in a shared stylesheet or design-system package is reused by name: a generic class (a wizard container class, a page header, a rejection-reason callout) goes onto a structurally or semantically different component, an app override targets a selector the DS package already styles, and a `.field + .field` rhythm rule or flex-column stretch default written for stacked children also fires on grid columns or inline buttons. Cascade order and specificity pick a winner silently, so a fix looks applied in one layout and fails in another, and each fix covers only the sibling shape that was reproduced first.
trigger_signals: a new component's root className matches a class already styled elsewhere in the same stylesheet or in a DS package
an app-level stylesheet overrides a selector also defined by a consumed shared/DS package
reusing a class named for another meaning (reason, error, danger) as a generic callout box
an adjacent-sibling (`.a + .b`) or descendant spacing rule in a stylesheet that also renders multi-column grid rows
a shared header/card class ported from a simpler portal into one that adds children (actions, buttons); a button placed directly inside a flex-column container
preventive_checks: Grep the class name across every stylesheet (app and DS package) before reusing or overriding it; give a new layout a modifier or component-specific class instead of relying on source order
When a CSS change doesn't apply, inspect computed styles for the winning rule and its source file before changing the selector; scope overrides by ANDing a component class onto the shared one
Scope rhythm rules to a stack container class; when fixing a `+`-combinator bug, enumerate every sibling shape that can follow the anchor and assert each one (top-edge delta for multi-column rows)
Set align-self or width explicitly for controls inside flex-column rows, and add position/size assertions (not only presence) for ported headers and action rows

FS-84.name: Dependency or toolchain change not resolved against what actually installs and runs
FS-84.mechanism: A package bump, override, version pin or tool-command migration is written as intent and never checked against the resolved result: a `>=` override lets pnpm jump a major version past the consumer's range, the pnpm that corepack resolves needs a newer Node than .nvmrc pins, a bump of the Playwright test package needs its matching browser binaries, and replacing `next lint` with `eslint .` silently widens the linted tree. The lockfile and the first run look fine until a fresh host, a fresh environment or a second verification pass hits it.
trigger_signals: adding a pnpm/npm override or resolution for a security patch
bumping the Playwright test package, Next, ESLint or another tool whose runtime assets or config format are coupled to its version
provisioning a host where Node/corepack is installed separately from the repo's .nvmrc and packageManager field
replacing a framework-scoped command (next lint) with a bare tool invocation (eslint .)
removing a package from requirements to escape a native-extension crash (cryptography SIGILL on an arm64 VM) while another installed package still imports it transitively (pymysql _auth)
preventive_checks: Write overrides as a caret range within the patched major (^4.3.2) and confirm the resolved version with pnpm why or the lockfile before committing
Pin packageManager explicitly and check that .nvmrc's Node satisfies the engines of the package manager and tools before provisioning
Make `playwright install` for the pinned version part of the bump commit's steps and of every fresh environment's pre-e2e setup; print tool versions before trusting lint/typecheck output
When migrating lint or type commands, re-create the old scope with explicit ignores and diff the error count against the pre-migration baseline
After removing a dependency, pip show / pip list inside the built image to confirm it is gone and run a bare import smoke test in a throwaway container on the target arch

FS-85.name: Status-gated behavior written for the states in view, not every value of the enum
FS-85.mechanism: UI and backend behavior keyed on a record's status (an action gate, a disabled button and the chip that explains it, a label map, the transition an action calls) is written and tested for the one or two states in the current design frame or ticket. Other values of the same enum fall through: a shared gate narrowed to one origin case hides Sign/Accept for another and deadlocks the flow, a button shown in several states calls a transition the backend table rejects from some of them (409), a disabled control has no status chip for the state that disables it, and a label map borrowed from another surface makes a pending state read as confirmed. Only the covered branch has e2e coverage, so users hit the rest in production.
trigger_signals: adding or narrowing a condition on a status/source enum inside a shared action-gate boolean during a UI or pixel-match pass
one UI action/button rendered in more than one record state but routed to a single transition endpoint
a control's enabled/disabled state depends on an enum while the chip/badge mapping was written earlier for fewer values
reusing an existing enum-to-label map from another page for a new design that specifies its own vocabulary
a shared failure/retry component reused for a second action but exposing a single retry callback
a new stage, document kind or job variant handled by an existing generic watchdog, stale-flag rule, label helper or recovery predicate
an idle, drain or availability check that lists 'active' run statuses explicitly while another feature adds a non-terminal status (woken, queued)
preventive_checks: List every value of the enum and write a state x action matrix (visible, enabled, which transition) before editing a gate; add one test per branch
For each state where the FE shows an action, check that the backend transition table allows the exact resulting transition and add an API test per state
Confirm every status that disables a control has a visible indicator explaining it
Diff each enum-to-label map against the design's vocabulary and assert the literal label text for every status in e2e
Test per failure kind that retry invokes the matching action

For each new variant, walk every generic handler of the enum (watchdog timeouts, stale rules, retry budgets, recovery predicates, reverse transitions such as orphaned -> live) and test the variant through each

FS-86.name: Hand-rolled CSS geometry trusted without a real render
FS-86.mechanism: Hand-written CSS layout (pseudo-element connector brackets, absolutely positioned children, repeating print headers, calc() height budgets) rests on layout mechanics the author assumed: the containing block (a missing position: relative), position: fixed in paged media anchoring to the page area inside the CSS page at-rule (page margins) rather than the sheet, a calc() constant that counts only the immediate parent's chrome, and a border shorthand in a :last-child override that clears both lines one pseudo-element draws. jsdom/RTL tests see DOM and text but no geometry, so the full suite is green while the rendered tree is off-centre, headers cover content, a connector vanishes or a scrollbar appears.
trigger_signals: a hand-rolled CSS tree/bracket/connector built from ::before/::after with absolute positioning, covered only by jsdom/RTL tests
a print/PDF layout uses position: fixed for a header or footer meant to repeat on every page, or enlarges the CSS page at-rule margin (page margins) to make room for it
a max-height/height: calc(100vh - Npx) on an inner scroller nested inside several padded or margined wrappers
a :first-child/:last-child override uses the border shorthand on a pseudo-element that draws two lines (border-top plus border-left)
preventive_checks: For any CSS layout claim (centring, connector lines, no page scroll, repeating header), verify in a real browser or PDF render with a geometric assertion (Playwright boundingBox or screenshot, scrollHeight === clientHeight, pdftotext -bbox on every page of a multi-page render) before calling it done; green jsdom tests are no evidence
Give the intended container of every absolutely positioned child or pseudo-element position: relative, and assert the rendered offset in the browser check
Repeat print headers and footers with display: table-header-group / table-footer-group, never position: fixed
Derive calc() budgets from the sum of every ancestor's padding, margin and border between the viewport edge and the element (or use flex with min-height: 0 instead of a magic constant)
When one pseudo-element draws two lines, override only the specific side (border-top: 0), never the border shorthand

FS-87.name: Non-standard account persona (store reviewer, shared demo, service) not modelled
FS-87.mechanism: Rules and flows are designed for the typical account: one real employee with the company SSO on their own device. One-approved-device-per-user, SSO-first login with credential login as a collapsed secondary link, and per-user session revocation all assume it. A store reviewer, shared demo/QA account or service identity breaks those assumptions: every login on the shared review account revokes the reviewer's device, the team's own smoke tests during review sign the reviewer out, and a reviewer without a company Google account never finds the fallback login. Everything passes for employees; store review rejects the build (Guideline 2.1) or reports 'session expired'.
trigger_signals: a per-user invariant (one device, one session, one active token) applies to an account type that is deliberately shared (store review, demo, QA, bot)
about to sign in repeatedly to, or smoke-test with, a shared production account such as the store review account while a review may be in progress
the app offers SSO plus a fallback credential login and the fallback renders as a de-emphasized or collapsed link
preparing a store submission that hands the reviewer demo credentials
preventive_checks: At design time list the non-standard account types (store reviewer, demo, QA, service) and give each an explicit exemption flag or isolated policy in the schema
Write a test that the shared/review account can hold N concurrent approved devices without revoking siblings, next to the single-user test
Never smoke-test with the live store review account; use a separate QA account under the same policy
Before every store submission walk the login flow on a fresh device as a user with no SSO account and confirm the fallback path is visible without prior knowledge

FS-88.name: Mobile OAuth client bound to a signing key or cloud project other than the one real installs use
FS-88.mechanism: Google Sign-In on Android binds the OAuth client to the package name plus the SHA-1 of the signing certificate, and requires that Android client to live in the same Google Cloud project as the webClientId used as the token audience. With Play App Signing, store installs are re-signed with a Google-held app-signing key whose SHA-1 differs from the local upload key, and an Android client created in another GCP project never matches the audience. Sideloaded and debug builds work; store installs fail with DEVELOPER_ERROR, which users report as a crash.
trigger_signals: enabling Play App Signing on an app that uses Google Sign-In or another SHA-1-bound Google API (Maps, Firebase)
creating a new Android/iOS OAuth client while the webClientId was created earlier, possibly in a different GCP project
Google Sign-In works on a sideloaded or debug build but a Play-installed build shows DEVELOPER_ERROR or 'not configured'
preventive_checks: Record the GCP project id of the webClientId and create every Android/iOS OAuth client in that same project; check it before registering any SHA-1

Register the SHA-1 of every key that signs a build users run: debug keystore, upload key and the Play app-signing key (Play Console App integrity, or apksigner verify on a Play-generated APK), as soon as Play App Signing is enabled
Test sign-in on a build installed from the Play internal track, not only a sideloaded APK, before promoting

FS-89.name: Derived counts, id lists and census docs not updated with their source collection
FS-89.mechanism: A source collection (benchmark cases, a ratchet/known-gap file, a retired-pin set) is mirrored elsewhere: generated coverage docs, a prose doc quoting its total, hardcoded `== {ids}` test literals, and a second id list in a DB-gated test. Changing the source leaves those copies stale. The scoped local gate doesn't cover them, so the drift shows up only in the full suite or in a CI-only job, often after review has passed.
trigger_signals: a change adds, removes or moves an entry in a source collection (benchmark case, ratchet/known-gap list, retired-pin set, registry) that docs or tests cite by count or id
the repo has generated coverage/census docs or a prose document quoting a total, with count-gate tests over them
a test asserts == {literal set of ids} or an exact count over a collection that is expected to grow
the gate that checks those artifacts runs only in CI (a Postgres-gated job) or in the full suite, not in the task's scoped selection
preventive_checks: After changing the source collection, run the doc/census generator, its count-gate tests and any doc checker (whitepapercheck) locally, then the full suite, not only the scoped selection
Grep tests/ and docs/ for the changed case id and the old count literal, including tests skipped locally because they need a DB, and update every hit in the same commit
Replace duplicated id sets and quoted totals with values derived from the source file, or assert a relational property (retired == declared-gone) instead of an exact literal
Put a local, no-DB check over every derived artifact (pre-push or unit test) so drift fails before CI

FS-90.name: Repo tooling bound to one machine's interpreter or to an unprovisioned worktree
FS-90.mechanism: Git hooks and test entry points hardcode an absolute interpreter path (a python.org framework build) or assume `python` is on PATH, and new worktrees ship without a venv. On another machine or worktree the hook can't start, or runs an interpreter that lacks native wheels and blocks by design. Each session then rediscovers which Python has pytest and the parsers, installs them by hand, and pushes with --no-verify.
trigger_signals: a committed git hook or script references an absolute interpreter path (/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/..., /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.x)
the first git push from this machine or worktree in the session
starting work in a fresh agent worktree checkout with no .venv and no `python` on PATH, on a host with several system Pythons
the hook needs native extension wheels (tree_sitter parsers) that only one installed interpreter has
e2e/backend scripts or spec helpers that resolve Python as <checkout>/.venv/bin/python run from a worktree with no venv
preventive_checks: Make hooks resolve the interpreter in order (repo .venv, then PATH python3) and check required imports up front with a clear message instead of a silent block
Ship one bootstrap command (make venv / scripts/setup) that builds the pinned-version venv with requirements plus test deps, and run it as step 0 in every new worktree
Before any documented --no-verify escape, run the exact gate the hook would run with the working venv and paste its green result into the PR body
After the second bypass, fix the hook on main instead of bypassing it again (FS-53)
Route every helper's interpreter through one resolver honoring an interpreter-override env variable, and create or link the venv as part of worktree creation

FS-91.name: Written claim in docs, comments or commit prose not re-derived from what it cites
FS-91.mechanism: Docstrings, whitepaper paragraphs, case source fields, adjudications and commit bodies state facts from the plan's prediction, from memory or from a copied note, not from a fresh run or a read of the source. Examples: 'this case now passes', 'this case proves end-to-end routing', a precedent's numbers, another file's note on wiring status. Reviewers catch the mismatch late, or it misdirects later planning.
trigger_signals: writing a docstring, comment or doc sentence saying a named test or case passes or proves a behavior
quoting another file's descriptive note (catalog notes, scope or wiring status) into new docs or a case's source field
a commit body, adjudication or PR description citing numbers, thresholds or commit history from another document
prose written in the same session as the plan that predicted the outcome
a hand-assembled .patch file or apply instruction committed into a report
preventive_checks: Run the exact test or case and cite its result next to any 'now passes' claim; if it still fails, write the outcome as expected, not achieved
Before describing what a case proves, trace the runner function it actually invokes and name that code path
Re-verify any quoted state note against current code instead of copying it
Open the cited document and quote its exact numbers and SHAs instead of paraphrasing from memory
Produce patch notes with git diff from a scratch branch and run git apply --check on a clean checkout before committing

FS-92.name: Integrity or result gate fails open on missing evidence or trips on non-canonical bytes
FS-92.mechanism: A guard or aggregator compares evidence it assumes is present and canonical. A truthy check lets a missing or blank recorded hash through. An aggregator that globs per-shard junit files reports a pass with a smaller denominator when a shard died before writing. A byte-hash guard over a zip that embeds mtimes rejects identical content, and a new optional field serialized unconditionally changes the hash of every old object. Happy-path tests, with inputs present and freshly built, never reach these edges.
trigger_signals: a guard shaped `if recorded and recorded != actual: raise`, or any integrity check whose recorded value can be absent
a report or aggregation step whose inputs change from one file per run to N per run (matrix, shards), or that globs artifacts by pattern
adding a sha/byte-identity guard around an archive or build step (zip, tar, zipapp)
adding a field to a model whose serialized form is hashed or signed
preventive_checks: Test missing, blank and corrupt inputs and assert the gate fails closed
Make aggregators assert the expected input count and each upstream job's outcome; simulate one shard producing no file and assert a failure, not a pass
Build the same source twice at different times and assert equal hashes before shipping a build-then-hash guard (normalize mtimes and order, or hash logical content)
When extending a hashed model, follow the existing empty-value-drop convention and run the hash-stability regression tests

FS-93.name: Live service config edited without a parse check and a post-restart re-read
FS-93.mechanism: Config for a running service is changed on a host and assumed to take effect and persist, whether through ALTER SYSTEM, a conf.d drop-in or postgresql.conf edited by an inline ssh command. A double-quoted value fails to parse and the server won't start. Nested quoting across ssh silently mangles the file. An ALTER SYSTEM value is lost when a package install triggers needrestart and bounces the service. The fallout appears later as 'database unreachable' and looks like an unrelated regression.
trigger_signals: writing a service config value via echo/heredoc or an inline ssh/sudo command with nested quotes
ALTER SYSTEM or another runtime-only setting followed by apt installs or other steps that can restart the service
a migration or provisioning session making several config edits on a production host in sequence
a secret written into .env as KEY=value #comment (unquoted inline comment on the value line), or any env value whose loader comment and quote rules are unverified
preventive_checks: Write config through a script file or a drop-in copied to the host, not multi-layer quoted inline commands
Validate before restarting with the service's own checker (postgres -C <setting> --config-file, nginx -t, a foreground start) and use the config language's quoting (single quotes in PostgreSQL)
Persist settings durably (conf.d drop-in) and re-read the effective value (SHOW <setting>, a health check that touches the DB) after every later install or restart step
Diff a failing ad hoc run against the verified harness path before trusting its failure count
Assert each loaded secret's length/prefix at startup (log the length, never the value) and lint .env files for text after the value before deploying

FS-94.name: CI fan-out multiplies load on a shared resource the single job never stressed
FS-94.mechanism: Splitting a job into a matrix of shards, or adding runners, multiplies whatever each job does. An auto-sized worker pool (xdist -n auto) in every shard oversubscribes the same cores. Per-job platform API calls (CreateArtifact, a setup action's version fetch) hit known-flaky endpoints N times at once. A flake fix tuned at the old concurrency fails again at the next increase. Per-shard timings look fine while wall clock and reliability get worse.
trigger_signals: a CI job gains a matrix/shard fan-out, or the self-hosted runner count increases
the sharded suite already parallelizes internally (pytest-xdist -n auto, jest workers)
steps after the test run call platform APIs (artifact upload, cache save, tool download) that the repo already notes as flaky
a concurrency-triggered flake was 'fixed' by tuning an input on the third-party action that makes the network call
preventive_checks: Cap per-shard workers at cores / shards (or keep one shard until shards run on separate hosts) and measure end-to-end wall clock before merging, not per-shard time
Audit every step after the test run for platform-API calls now made N times concurrently; add retry or continue-on-error to non-authoritative artifact uploads, keeping the job result authoritative
At each concurrency increase, re-run the scenario that flaked before, and prefer removing the network dependency (a host-provisioned tool) over tuning action inputs

FS-95.name: Worker-pool early-abort semantics assumed from the context manager
FS-95.mechanism: All work is submitted up front to a `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...)` block, and the code or a comment says a failure aborts the rest. But `__exit__` calls shutdown(wait=True) without cancel_futures, so every queued future still runs. Even with cancel_futures, a freed worker can grab one more queued item, so a test pinning an exact started-count flakes or fails deterministically.
trigger_signals: all work submitted to a `with ThreadPoolExecutor`/ProcessPoolExecutor block while a requirement says the first failure should stop the remaining work
a test or brief specifying an exact count of tasks started before cancellation
replacing a sequential loop that stopped at the first error with a pool
preventive_checks: Call pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=True) in a finally (or submit lazily), and test with more tasks than workers where task 0 raises, asserting started < total
Assert the guaranteed invariant (max in flight, started < total) rather than an exact count, and run the test 20+ times before trusting it
Compare how many tasks run on failure with the sequential loop being replaced

FS-96.name: Extracted document value trusted without a field-format check and an independent control total
FS-96.mechanism: OCR, vision or text extraction assigns a value to a field from a low-fidelity read (a downscaled multi-row tile) or from its position on the line (the leading numeric token) rather than from the field's defining format. Visually similar digits (33.00 vs 30.00) and neighbouring numeric fields (a 3-decimal pack size in the retail slot) are substituted silently. Only a reconciliation against a printed control total that happens to cover that field exposes it, and net-only checks miss gross or retail errors.
trigger_signals: a price, amount or quantity is read off a full-page or multi-row tile instead of a native-resolution crop of that single cell
a field is taken as 'the leading/Nth numeric token on the line' without checking its format (a currency slot showing 3 decimals)
the only reconciliation planned is against the net total while the document also prints gross, retail or group subtotals
preventive_checks: Re-read every extracted price/amount from a targeted native-resolution crop of its cell before accepting it

Validate each field's format before assigning it (currency has exactly 2 decimals; pack-size and quantity patterns differ) and send an explicit unknown (unit_retail: 0 for price-book resolution) instead of a guess
Reconcile every extracted column against each printed control it feeds: qty x price against gross and group subtotals, retail against the retail-dollar total, not only net

FS-97.name: Base branch changes behaviour a feature branch relies on, with no textual conflict
FS-97.mechanism: While a feature or integration branch is in flight, the base branch changes the behaviour of something it calls: a list/query service is re-scoped (a document list service narrowed to workspace members, so the bot principal sees nothing), a service the branch is rewriting gains new get semantics, a duplicate mechanism or new consumer of a shared component lands, or a module an e2e spec imports is removed. Git merges cleanly because the edits touch different lines, so the break surfaces only when the merged tree is tested, often after the branch was reported green.
trigger_signals: a feature or integration branch more than a day old whose base received merges touching services, managers, components or modules the branch calls
the branch rewrites or depends on a shared service (list/get scoping, annotations) or shared component while other tickets land on base
a principal other than a workspace member (bot, service account) reads through a shared list service
e2e specs import product modules from src/ instead of API/driver helpers
base merged into the branch cleanly and no tests were run afterwards
a stale branch hundreds of commits behind a base that upgraded tool majors (Vitest, lint plugins); two branches that each fixed the same spec's date/clock setup differently
preventive_checks: Merge the base branch into the feature/integration branch every wave (at least daily) and re-run the scoped tests and touched e2e specs on the merged tree before reporting green

Before merging, grep base's diff since the fork (git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/staging) origin/staging) for every service, manager, component and module your branch calls; read each behaviour change and pin the behaviour you rely on with a test
Pin cross-principal behaviour with one test per principal type (member user, bot, service account) on any shared service the branch reads through
Keep e2e specs on API/driver helpers, never product modules, and type-check tests/e2e after every merge
Before merging a stale branch diff package.json/tool majors between merge-base and base; after merging run git log origin/base -- <file> for every file touched on both sides and rerun those specs

FS-98.name: Desktop main-process windows, listeners and IPC state tied to one happy-path lifecycle
FS-98.mechanism: Electron main-process code assumes one window that lives as long as the app and a renderer that always answers. Listeners bind to the first window only, a lazy window accessor respawns windows during shutdown, fs watchers keep the process alive after quit, a 'recording' flag is cleared only by the renderer's success message, callback-contract handlers await with no error path, hidden windows have their timers throttled, isLoadingMainFrame is still true inside did-finish-load, a best-effort startup step aborts boot, the app's own HUD is still composited when frames are grabbed, and secondary windows sync auth but not the state that depends on it (or follow every later change). The single-window happy path works; quit, close-to-tray and reopen, renderer crash, a denied permission or a second window breaks it.
trigger_signals: main-process code attaching listeners, watchers, timers or IPC state to a BrowserWindow, or a change that lets windows close and be recreated (tray/dock keep-alive)
a state flag set on start and cleared only by a message from a renderer or another process
a callback-style Electron handler (display-media, permission) that awaits or has a deny/cancel branch
a timer, recorder or countdown hosted in a hidden or background window; a screen grab while the app's own HUD or hint windows may be visible
a filesystem/registry step in the startup path; navigation code that branches on isLoadingMainFrame from load events
a secondary window that mirrors main-window state through storage events or IPC
preventive_checks: For each main-process resource (window, listener, watcher, timer, IPC flag), list the events that end or recreate it (will-quit, close-to-tray and reopen, render-process-gone, hide) and test each: listeners re-bound on recreate, watchers closed on will-quit, no lazy respawn after before-quit, state back to idle on renderer death

Callback-contract handlers use try/finally so the callback fires exactly once, use a deny shape the pinned Electron major accepts, and are tested with process.on('unhandledRejection') failing the test
Windows that own timers set backgroundThrottling:false; hide the app's own chrome and wait for the compositor (or setContentProtection) before the first getSources
Wrap each best-effort startup step in its own try/catch and test with a throwing stub that the main window still opens; defer one tick from did-finish-load before reading load state

For cross-window sync, list every piece of state the secondary window derives from the main one (auth, workspace, dependent pickers) and decide per piece when it follows (sign-in only vs every switch); e2e sign-out/sign-in in window A and assert window B

FS-99.name: Document-parsing heuristic tuned on synthetic or single sample documents
FS-99.mechanism: Parsers and change detectors for real-world documents (Word BRDs through pandoc, meeting transcripts, minutes) are built against synthetic fixtures or tuned from one real sample: a colon-prefix speaker rule, a TOC line pattern, a heading-level rule, a noise-suppression skip rule. The next document differs (heading style != numbering, TOC kept as content, requirements authored as tables, a body that is all front matter, 'Action items:' headings), and the heuristic misreads or deletes real content. The real-document gate runs last, so the misfit surfaces at the end of the build.
trigger_signals: a spec names real-document risk for an import/parse feature while all fixtures are synthetic
changing a parsing heuristic because of one real document
a skip or strip rule keyed on a loose line pattern or an absence condition (no anchors, colon prefix, TOC-shaped line)
preventive_checks: Get several real documents at plan time (ask the user for customer samples) and run the real-document import gate from the first parser task, not in a final lane

Keep a corpus of edge-shaped fixtures (style != numbering, TOC, table-authored requirements, doc-control tables, an all-front-matter body, 'Heading:' lines) and run every heuristic change against all of them

Give every removal or skip heuristic a negative example, confirm matches against structure (TOC entries map to real headings) before deleting content, and guard a generalized fix with the condition of the sample it came from

FS-100.name: Async job result or system write applied without a current-state or supersession check
FS-100.mechanism: Bot/webhook callbacks, retried jobs and background subsystems write their result onto an entity without re-checking what it is now. A late callback mutates rows after the entity moved on, a retried job overwrites a newer version of a versioned aggregate, a completion writes a baseline from the snapshot captured at dispatch, and one subsystem overwrites another's blocked-reason field. Serial tests deliver each event once and in order, so late, duplicate and out-of-order arrivals corrupt state only in production-like runs.
trigger_signals: a bot/webhook callback endpoint or async job completion that writes shared rows and can arrive late, twice or after a retry
a versioned aggregate or review baseline written from data captured at dispatch time
several subsystems (watchdog, budget, bot failure, user hold) writing one status or reason field
a locally persisted draft restored over a field other users can save, or a tracker fed by both launch and resume events
preventive_checks: Capture a supersession token (job id, version, content hash) at dispatch; at apply time re-read the entity under a row lock and drop the result if status, version or hash no longer matches
Define a precedence order for shared status/reason slots and only overwrite a lower-precedence value
Test late, duplicate and out-of-order callbacks, and a completion arriving after a newer job was dispatched, asserting the newer state survives
Store the base version with a draft and warn or drop it when the server version moved; key trackers by entity id so a resume event applies idempotently

FS-101.name: Verification and review gates applied uniformly across a large multi-agent run
FS-101.mechanism: A multi-hour, multi-lane run applies the same heavy gate to every task: a whole-app suite (1000-2800 tests, 5-8 min under load) on every dispatch and fix round, Opus review plus re-review per task including minors, and final gates that re-run full suites and multi-viewport galleries already green on the same code. Subagents also issue test commands with new flags and env prefixes outside the pre-approved allowlist. The run spends most of its wall clock on redundant gates or stalls on permission prompts, and the load from redundant runs makes other lanes' tests flaky.
trigger_signals: a plan with dozens of tasks per lane and a per-task review plus re-review policy
a dispatch template that mandates a whole-app 'wide run' per task and per fix round
an exit-gate plan that repeats full-suite runs and screenshot galleries after every merge regardless of what changed
a long autonomous run whose subagents invoke pytest/vitest/playwright or scripts with varying env prefixes
preventive_checks: Tier gates by scope: scoped test files per task and fix round, the lane's suite once per wave, the full suite once on the final merged tree; re-run only what the change touched
Batch reviews per wave or by risk class and send minors to a follow-up list instead of fix rounds
Before launch, allowlist the exact command shapes subagents will run (test runners with their env prefixes and DB names) and put those exact commands in the briefs

FS-102.name: Performance lever chosen or credited without profiling, mechanism check or a controlled quiet-host A/B
FS-102.mechanism: Speed-up work picks a lever from a plan's premise (backend cost dominates, per-worker servers cap width, CONN_MAX_AGE pools connections, prepare_threshold caches plans) without a per-component time breakdown or a check that the mechanism is actually active at runtime, then judges it from single-shot wall-clock runs on a host shared with other lanes (load average 20-142). Inert levers get credited, real ones look like regressions, and ms budgets asserted inside a parallel suite fail by load, not code.
trigger_signals: a perf lane or brief assigns a lever to a layer (backend, DB driver, server count) before a per-test or per-request time breakdown exists
a settings comment or plan claims a driver/runtime option speeds things up (CONN_MAX_AGE under ASGI/Daphne, psycopg prepare_threshold, statement cache)
a before/after timing claim from one run each, on a machine where other agents, lanes or suites are running
several parallel lanes each asked to prove a speed-up with wall-clock benches on the same host
a test asserting a p95/ms budget that runs inside the default xdist/parallel suite or on shared CI hardware
preventive_checks: Profile one representative test or request first (API wall vs render/Vite vs setup, CPU per component at target width) and size the lever's ceiling before dispatching work on it

Prove the lever's mechanism is live before crediting it: pg_stat_database.sessions before/after N requests for connection reuse, pg_prepared_statements and EXPLAIN planning time for plan caching, the resolved settings module for config levers

Run A/B as interleaved pairs (ABBA/BAAB) from the same DB state under a host-wide bench lock, record load average per run, never run your own probes during a bench, and require the delta to exceed the spread of repeats
Gate perf in the main suite on query counts or other load-independent measures; move wall-clock ms budgets behind a marker run serially on a quiet host

FS-103.name: Column or renderer definitions rebuilt from volatile inputs remount the subtree
FS-103.mechanism: A table or list derives its column definitions, cell renderers or component types from volatile inputs (viewport width read in JS, a timer or flash state, inline handlers). When an input changes, even transiently, the UI framework sees new definition identities and remounts every cell, so local state inside them (an open menu, focus, an edit in progress) is dropped. Human testing at one stable width passes; resize events, transient layout values or a parallel suite surface it.
trigger_signals: column defs, cell renderers or component types computed inside render or memoized on viewport width, flash/timer state or inline callbacks
a JS width or matchMedia check choosing which columns or layout a table renders
an open menu, popover or inline editor that lives inside a table cell
preventive_checks: Switch layouts with CSS breakpoints instead of JS-chosen column sets
Keep column and renderer definitions identity-stable (module scope or memo with stable deps) and pass volatile values and handlers through context, table meta or refs
E2E: open the in-cell menu, fire a resize (including a transient tiny width) or the data/timer change, and assert the menu stays open

FS-104.name: Smoke or verification write run against a live production target
FS-104.mechanism: A smoke test or verification step performs a real write (deploy, publish, send) against a live production site or tenant because it is the closest real target. The write has side effects beyond the test itself, such as moving a public 'latest' alias or notifying users, so real visitors see test content. Read-only probes would not have changed anything; the side effect is noticed only by a later sweep or a user.
trigger_signals: a smoke, canary or go-live check that deploys, publishes or sends against an existing live site, tenant or channel
an operation that updates a shared pointer as a side effect (latest alias, default version, pinned release)
preventive_checks: Smoke-test writes against a dedicated throwaway target; use read-only probes on live targets
Before any write on a live target list its side effects (aliases, pointers, notifications) and diff the public state before and after

FS-105.name: Unattended agent fleet loses work at runtime boundaries with no durable replay, liveness sweep or idempotent recovery
FS-105.mechanism: A fleet of coding bots runs overnight: a server wakes each bot through a chat gateway, the bot runs a capped agent session in a worktree and reports back over one HTTP callback. Every boundary is fire-and-forget. A config or system-prompt re-render restarts the gateway and its drain drops inbound wakes with no replay; a 502 on the result callback leaves the session marked running and its slot held for an hour; a run hits its turn cap and waits for a human nobody is watching; the sweeper keeps retrying a known-broken path and exhausts its retry budget minutes before the fix lands. The human then recovers by hand (unassign/reassign loops, hand-written watchers), and non-idempotent recovery over-dispatches work that was already woken. Throughput is set by how fast someone notices, not by the bots.
trigger_signals: bots woken by chat messages or webhooks with no server-side record of unacknowledged wakes
a run reports completion through a single HTTP callback with no retry, heartbeat or stale-slot reaper
a server-side change (system-prompt re-render, config) that restarts the bot gateway while lanes are live
unattended agent runs with a turn or budget cap below the task size
recovering lost work by toggling assignment or status in a loop
deploying a fix to a path an automated sweep or retry loop is still hitting
an overnight or multi-hour fleet run supervised only by a human or by ad hoc watchers
preventive_checks: Before the first unattended night, make every hop durable: wakes queued server-side and replayed until acknowledged, result callbacks retried, live runs heartbeated, and a timer sweep that reaps stale slots and re-wakes lost work
Recovery must be idempotent: re-wake only items confirmed lost through an explicit re-wake call, never by unassign/reassign loops; assert the wake count stays under the lane cap
Auto-continue runs that stop on a turn or budget cap up to a lane budget, then escalate to a human instead of idling
Pause the sweep or reset its retry counters before deploying a fix to the path it retries
Run one supervision loop on a schedule (launchd/systemd or a scheduled agent) that checks every lane's state, heartbeat age and queue, instead of hand-written watchers per incident

FS-106.name: Test-result reporting collapses, filters or duplicates results so the run's verdict misstates what executed
FS-106.mechanism: Automated test results flow from a runner (JUnit, Playwright JSON) through a push CLI into a test-management ingest that maps many tests to one case. Each hop silently reshapes the verdict: ingest keeps one result per case (highest attempt, first on tie) so a failing test hides behind a passing one; a scoped run serializes every filtered-out test as skipped, and the UI counts skipped as complete, so 6 passed out of 182 reads as 100%; the scoped command runs one runner and misses e2e specs tagged to the same case; a wrapper pushes twice and creates duplicate runs; an evidence flag uploads nothing without its companion flag. Requirements turn green on evidence that does not exist.
trigger_signals: many automated tests mapped to one test case or requirement (case-id tags, name patterns)
a dedupe or winner-selection step in a result ingest keyed on attempt, order or timestamp
a scoped or filtered test run (-t, --grep, tag filter) whose report is pushed as a run
case tags spread across several runners (unit, API e2e, browser e2e) while the scoped command calls one
a QA bot or CI wrapper that pushes results and may retry or be invoked twice
progress or coverage percentages that count skipped as executed
preventive_checks: Collapse many results per case with worst-result-wins (failed > blocked > passed > skipped) within and across chunks, and test a case with one passing and one failing test
Push only executed tests from a scoped run (or flag the run as scoped); keep skipped distinct from untested and exclude skipped from pass percentages
Build the scoped command from every runner's specs tagged to the case and assert the executed count matches the tagged count
Make result pushes idempotent on an external run id and assert one run per ticket round
After a push, read the run back: totals, executed vs skipped, evidence count, and compare them with the runner's own summary

FS-107.name: New obligation or notification enabled by default for existing callers
FS-107.mechanism: A finalize step, a new notification type or a new background check becomes active by default for every caller or existing user: a pending obligation (an expected upload, an acknowledgement) that a timer later escalates, or a new event that a stored wildcard preference or master switch opts everyone into. Callers that never intended to take part create stalled records, false alarms and auto-filed tickets, or existing users start receiving messages they never asked for. Opt-out defaults hide it until the timer fires or the deploy reaches production.
trigger_signals: a finalize, close or submit step that creates a pending record a sweeper later escalates or notifies on
a boolean like *_expected / *_required defaulting to true, or inferred from weak signals
a new notification or event type evaluated against stored wildcard or master-switch preferences ({*: true})
preventive_checks: Make the obligation opt-in by the caller that will fulfil it; default off
Test that the plain path (no opt-in) creates nothing pending and never escalates; a late fulfilment may reopen it
Test an existing user's stored preferences (wildcards, master switch) against the new event and assert the documented default wins

FS-108.name: Non-production deploy acts on production data through a shared store
FS-108.mechanism: Staging and production share one database, queue or outbox, so any worker, sweep or drain deployed to staging runs against production rows and posts to production integrations (chat, email, webhooks). A new sweep designed as if it runs only at the production deploy releases an accumulated backlog, such as weeks-old messages, to real users the moment staging deploys. Tests run on an isolated DB, so the cross-environment reach shows up only in review or in production.
trigger_signals: a new worker, sweep, drain or reconcile job over a table, queue or outbox that more than one environment reads
the first run of a new sweep over rows that accumulated before it existed
an environment whose settings point at another environment's database, broker or integration credentials
preventive_checks: Before shipping a worker, list every environment that runs it against the same store and every external endpoint it posts to; gate its side effects to the environment that owns the rows (an environment flag or an owner column)
Bound the first run: dry-run count the rows it would act on, skip items older than a cutoff, and release any backlog deliberately

FS-109.name: Waiting state with no deadline when its resolver disappears
FS-109.mechanism: A record or process enters a waiting state (pending, updating, held, mismatch) whose only exit is an event from another actor: a watcher, a callback, a renderer or a follow-up flow. When that actor dies, restarts or is never started, nothing moves the state on and it holds forever: a node stops sending heartbeats, a run never settles, a badge says updating indefinitely. Tests always drive the resolver, so the never-resolves path is first exercised live.
trigger_signals: a new pending, held or verifying state that is cleared only by another process, callback or user action
a hold that suppresses a liveness signal (heartbeat, lease renewal) until a check passes
a watcher or supervisor process that may be absent after a restart or an upgrade
preventive_checks: For every waiting state write down the event that ends it and a deadline that moves it to a reported terminal state (failed, rolled back)
Test the resolver never arriving: kill the watcher or drop the callback, advance the clock past the deadline, and assert the state ends and liveness resumes

FS-110.name: Admission gate decides on a load sample that lags admitted work
FS-110.mechanism: A gate admits heavy jobs (parallel agent lanes, test runs, builds) when one instantaneous sample of CPU idle or load looks healthy. Jobs admitted moments earlier have not ramped up yet, so the sample still reads idle and several jobs pass together; when they ramp at once the host thrashes (load far above the core count, agents stall). Background OS work such as file indexing of new checkouts adds to it. Each admission looked correct when it was made.
trigger_signals: an admission or throttle gate that checks current CPU idle, load average or free memory once before starting each job
jobs that take minutes to reach peak usage (dependency install, server boot, test-suite ramp)
several queued jobs waiting on the same gate
preventive_checks: Count admitted-but-ramping jobs against the budget (a fixed reservation per admission for its ramp window) instead of trusting the live sample alone
Admit one job at a time with a cooldown about as long as a job's ramp, decide on a sampled window rather than one reading, and keep a hard cap on concurrent heavy jobs
